scenarios.title_en: Check-in: an overweight bag

situation.en: You're at the airport in London, checking in for your flight home to Tel Aviv. Your suitcase goes on the scale, and it's 4 kilos over the limit on your ticket. (Prices in this scenario are made-up examples.)
situation.he: אתם בשדה התעופה בלונדון, בצ'ק-אין לטיסה הביתה לתל אביב. אתם מניחים את המזוודה על המשקל, ומתברר שהיא חורגת ב-4 קילו מהמותר בכרטיס שלכם. (המחירים בתרחיש הם דוגמה בלבד.)

goal.en: Find out your options (pay a fee or repack), choose one politely and finish checking in.
goal.he: לברר מה האפשרויות (לשלם תוספת או להעביר חפצים), לבחור אחת מהן בנימוס ולסיים את הצ'ק-אין.

phrases.en: Hi, I'd like to check in for my flight to Tel Aviv, please.
phrases.he: שלום, אשמח לעשות צ'ק-אין לטיסה לתל אביב.

phrases.en: How much over the limit is it?
What's the excess baggage fee?
phrases.he: כמה עולה התשלום על משקל עודף?
phrases.note: 'Excess baggage' is the term airlines use for extra weight or extra bags.

phrases.en: Is there any flexibility on the weight?
phrases.note: A polite way to ask them to let it go. Don't expect a yes.

phrases.en: Can I move a few things into my carry-on?
phrases.he: אפשר להעביר כמה דברים למטען היד?

phrases.en: Can I move a few things into my hand luggage?
phrases.he: אפשר להעביר כמה דברים למטען היד?

phrases.en: Is it OK if I repack over there?
phrases.he: זה בסדר אם אסדר את המזוודה מחדש שם בצד?

phrases.en: I'll just pay the fee, that's fine.
phrases.he: אני פשוט אשלם את התוספת, זה בסדר.

phrases.en: No problem, just give me a sec.
phrases.note: 'A sec' = a second. Fine with friendly staff.

phrases.en: Could I have an aisle seat, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל מושב ליד המעבר, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Which gate is it, and what time does boarding start?
phrases.he: מאיזה שער יוצאים, ומתי מתחילה העלייה למטוס?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hello. Where are you flying to today?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi, Tel Aviv. Here's my passport.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Thank you. Could you put your suitcase on the scale, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sure, here you go.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Right, it's 27 kilos. Your ticket allows 23, so you're 4 kilos over, I'm afraid.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh no. How much is the fee for the extra weight?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's £65. Or you can move some things into your hand luggage, if you've got room.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I think I'll repack. Is it OK if I do it over there?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. Just come straight back to me when you're done. No need to queue again.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thanks. I'll be quick.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Perfect, 23 kilos exactly. Here's your boarding pass: gate 14, boarding at 10:40.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thanks so much. Have a good day.

practice.partner: Hello. Where are you flying to today?

options.text: To Tel Aviv. Quick, I'm late.

feedback.en: Sounds rude. If you're short on time, say 'Sorry, I'm in a bit of a hurry.'
feedback.he: נשמע גס. אם אתם לחוצים בזמן, אפשר לומר: Sorry, I'm in a bit of a hurry.

options.text: Hi, Tel Aviv. Here's my passport.

feedback.en: Natural and efficient: you answer and hand over your passport in one go.
feedback.he: טבעי ויעיל: עונים על השאלה ומגישים את הדרכון באותו משפט.

options.text: I am flying to Tel Aviv today.

feedback.en: Correct, but a bit stiff. People usually just say the place.
feedback.he: נכון דקדוקית, אבל קצת נוקשה. בדרך כלל פשוט אומרים את היעד.

model_replies: Hi, Tel Aviv. Here's my passport.
Hello, I'm going to Tel Aviv. Here you go.

practice.partner: Right, it's 27 kilos. Your ticket allows 23, so you're 4 kilos over, I'm afraid.

options.text: Oh, I see. How much would the extra weight cost?

feedback.en: Calm and polite. 'Would' makes the question softer.
feedback.he: רגוע ומנומס. would מרכך את השאלה.

options.text: What is the price for this?

feedback.en: Understandable, but vague and a bit flat. Say what you mean: 'the extra weight' or 'the fee'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל כללי ויבש. עדיף לפרט: the extra weight או the fee.

options.text: That's not my problem. Your scale is wrong.

feedback.en: Arguing with the agent won't help and sounds aggressive. Ask about your options instead.
feedback.he: ויכוח עם הנציג לא יעזור ונשמע תוקפני. עדיף לשאול מה האפשרויות.

model_replies: Oh, I see. How much would the extra weight cost?
Oh no. What are my options?
Sorry, I didn't know. How much is the fee?

practice.partner: It's £65. Or you can move some things into your hand luggage, if you've got room.

options.text: I want to put things in my bag.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'I want' sounds abrupt in English. 'I'll' or 'I'd like to' is softer.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל I want נשמע ישיר מדי באנגלית. I'll או I'd like to רכים יותר.

options.text: No, I don't pay. You do it free.

feedback.en: Rude and ungrammatical. If you want to ask for a little flexibility, do it nicely: 'Is there any flexibility?'
feedback.he: גס ולא תקין דקדוקית. אם רוצים לבקש הקלה, עושים את זה בנימוס: Is there any flexibility?

options.text: I'll move a few things, then. Is it OK if I repack over there?

feedback.en: A clear decision, then a polite check before you step aside.
feedback.he: החלטה ברורה, ואחריה בקשת רשות מנומסת לפני שזזים הצידה.

model_replies: I'll move a few things, then. Is it OK if I repack over there?
I think I'll repack. Can I do it over there?

practice.partner: Perfect, 23 kilos. Would you like a window or an aisle seat?

options.text: I want the seat near the way.

feedback.en: 'The way' doesn't work here. The seat next to the walkway is called an 'aisle seat'.
feedback.he: the way לא מתאים כאן. המושב ליד המעבר נקרא aisle seat.

options.text: An aisle seat, please, if there's one left.

feedback.en: Polite and natural. 'If there's one left' shows you know it might not be available.
feedback.he: מנומס וטבעי. if there's one left מראה שאתם מבינים שאולי אין כבר מקום פנוי.

options.text: Aisle.

feedback.en: Fine in a quick exchange, but adding 'please' makes it much friendlier.
feedback.he: בסדר בשיחה מהירה, אבל עם please זה נשמע הרבה יותר נעים.

model_replies: An aisle seat, please.
Window, please, if there's one left.
I'd prefer an aisle seat, please.

practice.partner: Here's your boarding pass. Gate 14, and boarding starts at 10:40.

options.text: Great, thanks. Is the gate far from security?

feedback.en: A natural thank-you plus a useful follow-up question.
feedback.he: תודה טבעית ושאלת המשך שימושית.

options.text: Thank you very much for all your kind help, I appreciate it a lot.

feedback.en: Polite, but more than a quick check-in needs. 'Thanks so much' is enough.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל יותר ממה שצ'ק-אין קצר דורש. Thanks so much מספיק.

options.text: OK. Bye.

feedback.en: Correct, but it sounds cold after the agent has helped you. Add a 'thanks'.
feedback.he: תקין, אבל נשמע קר אחרי שעזרו לכם. כדאי להוסיף thanks.

model_replies: Great, thanks. Is the gate far from security?
Thanks so much. Have a good day.

roleplay.persona: Margaret, a check-in agent at a London airport. Experienced and friendly, but firm about the rules; she has heard every excuse about heavy bags.
roleplay.complication: The bag is 4 kilos over. After the learner repacks, it's still half a kilo over. Margaret only lets it go if the learner asks politely, and she warns that hand luggage has its own weight limit.
roleplay.opening_line: Hello! Where are you off to today? Could you pop your case on the scale for me?

culture.en: Baggage allowances and fees depend on the airline and the ticket type. Check them in your booking before you fly.
culture.he: המשקל המותר והתעריפים משתנים לפי חברת התעופה וסוג הכרטיס. כדאי לבדוק אותם בהזמנה לפני הטיסה.

culture.en: Check-in agents rarely bend the rules, but a friendly tone sometimes gets you a little flexibility. Arguing almost never does.
culture.he: נציגי צ'ק-אין חורגים מהכללים רק לעתים רחוקות, אבל טון נעים מביא לפעמים קצת גמישות. ויכוח כמעט אף פעם לא עוזר.

variants.note: The bag you take on the plane with you.
'Get in line' (US) / 'join the queue' (UK).

scenarios.title_en: Passport control and customs on arrival

situation.en: You've just landed in New York for a two-week trip. At passport control, an officer checks your passport and asks you a few questions. Then, at customs, another officer asks what you're bringing in.
situation.he: נחתתם עכשיו בניו יורק לטיול של שבועיים. בביקורת הדרכונים בודקים את הדרכון ושואלים אתכם כמה שאלות, ואחר כך במכס שואלים מה אתם מכניסים למדינה.

goal.en: Answer the officers' questions clearly, briefly and truthfully.
goal.he: לענות על השאלות בצורה ברורה, קצרה וכנה.

phrases.en: I'm here on vacation for two weeks.
I'm here on holiday for two weeks.
I'm visiting my cousins in Brooklyn.
phrases.he: באתי לבקר את בני הדודים שלי בברוקלין.

phrases.en: I'm staying at the Park Hotel in Manhattan.
phrases.note: Stay AT a hotel, stay WITH a person.

phrases.en: Here's my hotel booking, if you need it.
phrases.he: הנה אישור ההזמנה מהמלון, אם צריך.

phrases.en: It's my first time in the US.
phrases.he: זו הפעם הראשונה שלי בארצות הברית.

phrases.en: My return flight is on the 20th.
Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
No, nothing to declare.
I have some snacks from home. Do I need to declare them?
phrases.he: יש לי כמה חטיפים מהבית. צריך להצהיר עליהם?

phrases.en: Just clothes and a few presents.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Good morning. Passport, please... Thanks. What's the purpose of your visit?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Tourism. I'm here on vacation.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: How long are you staying?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Two weeks. I fly back on the 20th.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: And where are you staying?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: At the Park Hotel in Manhattan. I have the booking here if you need it.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: That's fine. Look at the camera, please... Thank you. Enjoy your stay.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thank you!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi there. Anything to declare? Any food, fruit or plants?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Just some chocolate and snacks from home. Do I need to declare them?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let me take a look... That's fine. Go ahead.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thanks. Have a nice day.

practice.partner: What's the purpose of your visit?

options.text: The purpose of my visit is tourism.

feedback.en: Correct, but repeating the whole question sounds stiff. A short answer is more natural.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל חזרה על כל השאלה נשמעת נוקשה. תשובה קצרה טבעית יותר.

options.text: Why do you ask? That's my business.

feedback.en: Never challenge a border officer. These are routine questions, so just answer them.
feedback.he: אף פעם לא מתעמתים עם פקיד הגבול. אלה שאלות שגרתיות, ופשוט עונים עליהן.

options.text: Tourism. I'm here on vacation for two weeks.

feedback.en: Short, clear and complete: the reason plus how long you're staying.
feedback.he: קצר, ברור ומלא: הסיבה וגם משך השהייה.

model_replies: Tourism. I'm here on vacation.
I'm visiting family for two weeks.
Tourism. I'm here for two weeks.

practice.partner: How long are you staying?

options.text: I stay two week.

feedback.en: Wrong tense and a missing plural. Say 'I'm staying for two weeks.'
feedback.he: זמן הפועל שגוי וחסרה צורת הרבים. אומרים: I'm staying for two weeks.

options.text: Two weeks. I fly back on the 20th.

feedback.en: Precise, and the return date shows you have a ticket home.
feedback.he: תשובה מדויקת, ותאריך החזרה מראה שיש לכם כרטיס הביתה.

options.text: Maybe two weeks, maybe a bit more. I'm not sure.

feedback.en: Honest, but vague answers can lead to more questions. If you have a return date, give it.
feedback.he: כנה, אבל תשובה מעורפלת עלולה להוביל לעוד שאלות. אם יש לכם תאריך חזרה, ציינו אותו.

model_replies: Two weeks. I fly back on the 20th.
I'm staying for two weeks.

practice.partner: Where are you staying?

options.text: At the Park Hotel in Manhattan. I have the booking here if you need it.

feedback.en: Specific and helpful. Offering the booking shows you're prepared.
feedback.he: ספציפי ומועיל. ההצעה להראות את ההזמנה מראה שאתם מוכנים.

options.text: In a hotel.

feedback.en: True, but too vague. Officers usually want the name or the address.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל כללי מדי. בדרך כלל רוצים לשמוע את שם המלון או את הכתובת.

options.text: I don't know yet. I'll find something.

feedback.en: This can cause trouble at the border. Always have an address ready, at least for the first night.
feedback.he: תשובה כזאת עלולה לעורר בעיה בגבול. תמיד כדאי שתהיה כתובת מוכנה, לפחות ללילה הראשון.

model_replies: At the Park Hotel in Manhattan.
With my cousins in Brooklyn. I have their address here.

practice.partner: Is this your first visit to the United States?

options.text: Yes, it is my first visit to the United States.

feedback.en: Correct, but repeating the question sounds stiff. 'It's my first time' is lighter.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל החזרה על השאלה נשמעת נוקשה. It's my first time קליל יותר.

options.text: Yes, I never was here before.

feedback.en: Wrong tense and word order. Say 'I've never been here before.'
feedback.he: זמן הפועל וסדר המילים שגויים. אומרים: I've never been here before.

options.text: Yes, it's my first time here.

feedback.en: Short and natural. 'It's my first time' is the usual way to say it.
feedback.he: קצר וטבעי. It's my first time היא הדרך הרגילה לומר את זה.

model_replies: Yes, it's my first time.
No, I was here three years ago.

practice.partner: Do you have anything to declare? Any food, fruit or plants?

options.text: Nothing special. Why, do I look suspicious?

feedback.en: Jokes and defensive questions are a bad idea at customs. Answer the question directly.
feedback.he: בדיחות ושאלות מתגוננות הן רעיון רע במכס. עונים ישירות על השאלה.

options.text: Just some chocolate and snacks from home. Do I need to declare them?

feedback.en: Honest and sensible: when you're not sure, mention it and ask.
feedback.he: כנה והגיוני: כשלא בטוחים, מציינים ושואלים.

options.text: No.

feedback.en: Fine if it's true. But if you do have food, say so: hiding it can get you into trouble.
feedback.he: בסדר אם זה נכון. אבל אם יש לכם אוכל, צריך לומר את זה. הסתרה עלולה לסבך אתכם.

model_replies: Just some chocolate and snacks. Do I need to declare them?
No, nothing to declare.
I have some snacks from home. Is that OK?

roleplay.persona: Officer Ruiz, an immigration officer at a New York airport. Professional and brief, rarely smiles but isn't unfriendly; asks short questions and expects short, clear answers.
roleplay.complication: The learner's hotel booking starts the day after they land. Officer Ruiz notices and asks where they're sleeping tonight; the learner has to explain clearly (for example, a night with a friend) and give an address.
roleplay.opening_line: Next! Passport, please... Thank you. What brings you to the United States?

culture.en: Never joke at passport control, customs or security. Officers have to take every comment seriously, jokes included.
culture.he: אף פעם לא מתבדחים בביקורת הדרכונים, במכס או בבידוק הביטחוני. הפקידים חייבים להתייחס ברצינות לכל משפט, גם לבדיחה.

culture.en: Answer briefly and truthfully. You don't need long explanations, but have your return date and accommodation address ready.
culture.he: עונים בקצרה ובכנות. אין צורך בהסברים ארוכים, אבל כדאי שיהיו מוכנים תאריך החזרה וכתובת מקום הלינה.

culture.en: Entry rules (visas, electronic travel permits, which foods you can bring in) differ from country to country and change over time. Check the official government website before you travel.
culture.he: כללי הכניסה (ויזה, אישור נסיעה אלקטרוני, אילו מזונות מותר להכניס) שונים ממדינה למדינה ומשתנים מעת לעת. כדאי לבדוק באתר הממשלתי הרשמי לפני הנסיעה.

variants.note: Sweet baked snacks. In the US, a 'biscuit' is a soft bread roll, a bit like a scone.

scenarios.title_en: Delayed flight: getting rebooked

situation.en: You're flying from Madrid to New York with a connection in London. Your flight to London is delayed by three hours, so you're going to miss your connection. You go to the airline's service desk.
situation.he: אתם טסים ממדריד לניו יורק עם החלפת מטוס בלונדון. הטיסה ללונדון מתעכבת בשלוש שעות, כך שתפספסו את טיסת ההמשך. אתם ניגשים לדלפק השירות של חברת התעופה.

goal.en: Explain the problem, get rebooked onto the best alternative and check what happens to your bag.
goal.he: להסביר את הבעיה, לעבור לטיסה החלופית הטובה ביותר ולברר מה יקרה עם המזוודה.

phrases.en: My flight's been delayed, and I'm going to miss my connection.
phrases.he: הטיסה שלי מתעכבת, ואפספס את טיסת ההמשך.

phrases.en: Could you rebook me on another flight, please?
phrases.he: אפשר להעביר אותי לטיסה אחרת, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Is there anything earlier, even with another airline?
phrases.he: יש משהו מוקדם יותר, אפילו בחברה אחרת?

phrases.en: I'd rather not wait until tomorrow, if there's another option.
phrases.he: אעדיף לא לחכות עד מחר, אם יש אפשרות אחרת.
phrases.note: 'I'd rather not' is a soft way to say no.

phrases.en: Will I have to pay anything extra?
Will my checked bag be transferred automatically?
phrases.he: המזוודה שלי תועבר לטיסה החדשה אוטומטית?

phrases.en: Do you provide meal vouchers for the delay?
phrases.he: אתם נותנים שוברי ארוחה בגלל העיכוב?

phrases.en: If I have to stay overnight, will you arrange a hotel?
phrases.he: אם אצטרך ללון כאן, תסדרו לי מלון?

phrases.en: Could I get that in writing, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל את זה בכתב, בבקשה?

phrases.en: OK, that works for me.
Is this the line for rebooking?
Is this the queue for rebooking?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi. My flight to London is delayed by three hours, so I'm going to miss my connection to New York.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: I'm sorry about that. Can I see your passport and boarding pass?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sure, here you go.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: OK... The next connection I can get you on is tomorrow morning at 9:15. Would that work?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I'd rather not wait until tomorrow, if there's another option. Is there anything tonight, even with another airline?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let me check... There's a direct flight from here to New York at 6:30 this evening with one of our partners. It's quite full, but I can get you a middle seat.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: That would be great. Will I have to pay anything extra?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No, there's no charge, since the delay is on our side.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. And what about my checked bag?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It hasn't been loaded yet, so we'll move it to the new flight. Here's your new boarding pass, and a meal voucher for the wait.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thank you so much. I really appreciate your help.

practice.partner: Hi, how can I help?

options.text: Hi. My flight to London is delayed, so I'm going to miss my connection. Could you help me rebook?

feedback.en: Ideal: the problem, the result and a clear request, in that order.
feedback.he: מצוין: הבעיה, התוצאה ובקשה ברורה, לפי הסדר.

options.text: My flight is late. I need a new flight.

feedback.en: Understandable, but abrupt, and it doesn't explain why you need a new flight (the connection).
feedback.he: מובן, אבל קצר ויבש, ולא מסביר למה צריך טיסה חדשה (טיסת ההמשך).

options.text: Your airline is a disaster! Fix this now.

feedback.en: Anger won't make the agent work faster, and the delay isn't their personal fault. Stay calm and specific.
feedback.he: כעס לא יגרום לנציג לעבוד מהר יותר, והעיכוב הוא לא אשמתו האישית. עדיף להישאר רגועים ולדייק.

model_replies: Hi. My flight to London is delayed, so I'm going to miss my connection. Could you help me rebook?
Hi, I'm going to miss my connecting flight because of the delay. What are my options?

practice.partner: The next connection I can get you on is tomorrow morning at 9:15. Would that work?

options.text: No, tomorrow is not good for me.

feedback.en: Clear, but it closes the conversation. Ask about alternatives so the agent knows what to look for.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל סוגר את השיחה. כדאי לשאול על חלופות, כדי שהנציג יידע מה לחפש.

options.text: Tomorrow? Are you joking?

feedback.en: Sarcasm sounds rude and makes the agent less keen to help.
feedback.he: עוקצנות נשמעת גסה ומורידה לנציג את החשק לעזור.

options.text: I'd rather not wait until tomorrow, if there's another option. Is there anything tonight, even with another airline?

feedback.en: Polite but persistent. 'I'd rather not' is a soft way to say no, and you suggest a solution.
feedback.he: מנומס אבל נחוש. I'd rather not היא דרך רכה לומר לא, ואתם גם מציעים פתרון.

model_replies: I'd rather not wait until tomorrow. Is there anything tonight?
Is there anything earlier, even with another airline?

practice.partner: There's a flight to New York at 6:30 this evening with one of our partners. It's quite full, but I can get you a middle seat.

options.text: A middle seat? No way. Give me business class.

feedback.en: Demanding an upgrade isn't realistic here. You can ask, but politely: 'Is there any chance of an aisle seat?'
feedback.he: לדרוש שדרוג זה לא מציאותי כאן. אפשר לבקש, אבל בנימוס: Is there any chance of an aisle seat?

options.text: That would be great, thanks. A middle seat is fine.

feedback.en: Accepting graciously. 'That would be great' is the natural way to say yes to an offer.
feedback.he: קבלה אדיבה של ההצעה. That would be great היא הדרך הטבעית לומר כן להצעה.

options.text: Yes. Book it.

feedback.en: It works, but it sounds like an order. Add 'please' or 'that would be great'.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל נשמע כמו פקודה. כדאי להוסיף please או that would be great.

model_replies: That would be great, thanks. A middle seat is fine.
Yes, please. Is there any chance of an aisle seat?

practice.partner: OK, you're booked on the 6:30 flight. Anything else?

options.text: Yes, will my checked bag go on the new flight automatically?

feedback.en: An important question: after any change, always check what happens to your luggage.
feedback.he: שאלה חשובה: אחרי כל שינוי כדאי לברר מה קורה עם המזוודה.

options.text: And my bag?

feedback.en: Understandable in context, but a full question is clearer and more polite.
feedback.he: מובן בהקשר, אבל שאלה מלאה ברורה ומנומסת יותר.

options.text: Where is my bag go?

feedback.en: Mixed-up grammar. Say 'Where will my bag go?' or 'What happens to my bag?'
feedback.he: ערבוב דקדוקי. אומרים Where will my bag go? או What happens to my bag?

model_replies: Yes, will my checked bag go on the new flight automatically?
Just one thing: what happens to my luggage?

practice.partner: Your bag will be moved to the new flight. And here's a meal voucher for the wait.

options.text: OK, thanks. How much is the voucher for?

feedback.en: A fair, practical question. But a quick 'OK, thanks' sounds a little flat after all the agent's help, so thank them properly first.
feedback.he: שאלה מעשית ולגיטימית. אבל OK, thanks בלבד נשמע קצת יבש אחרי כל העזרה, אז קודם מודים כמו שצריך.

options.text: Only a voucher? That's nothing.

feedback.en: Ungrateful, and it won't get you more. If you think you're owed more, calmly ask about the airline's policy.
feedback.he: נשמע כפוי טובה, וזה לא יביא לכם יותר. אם נראה לכם שמגיע לכם יותר, שאלו ברוגע על מדיניות החברה.

options.text: Thank you so much. I really appreciate your help.

feedback.en: Warm and natural. Agents on a busy delay day remember polite passengers.
feedback.he: חם וטבעי. ביום עמוס בעיכובים, נציגים זוכרים נוסעים מנומסים.

model_replies: Thank you so much. I really appreciate your help.
Thanks a lot. You've been really helpful.

roleplay.persona: Stefan, an airline agent at Madrid airport. Tired after a long shift full of delayed passengers, but genuinely helpful to anyone who stays calm and clear.
roleplay.complication: The only same-day option lands in New York at 1 a.m., and the learner's checked bag might not make it onto that flight. The learner has to choose: arrive tonight without a guarantee about the bag, or fly tomorrow with a hotel night provided.
roleplay.opening_line: Next, please! Sorry about the wait, it's been a busy afternoon. How can I help?

culture.en: Passenger rights after a delay (meals, a hotel, compensation) depend on the country, the airline and the reason for the delay. Ask politely what applies to you, and keep your boarding passes and receipts.
culture.he: זכויות הנוסעים בעיכוב (ארוחות, מלון, פיצוי) תלויות במדינה, בחברת התעופה ובסיבת העיכוב. שאלו בנימוס מה חל עליכם, ושמרו את כרטיסי העלייה למטוס ואת הקבלות.

culture.en: Staff at a busy desk respond best to calm, specific requests. Know what you want before you reach the front of the line.
culture.he: נציגים בדלפק עמוס מגיבים הכי טוב לבקשות רגועות ומדויקות. כדאי לדעת מה רוצים לפני שמגיעים לראש התור.

variants.note: The bag that travels in the hold, not in the cabin. 'Checked luggage' is understood everywhere.

scenarios.title_en: Reporting lost luggage

situation.en: You've just landed in Manchester after flying from Tel Aviv via Frankfurt. Everyone else has collected their bags, but yours never came out. You go to the baggage services desk.
situation.he: נחתתם עכשיו במנצ'סטר, אחרי טיסה מתל אביב דרך פרנקפורט. כל שאר הנוסעים כבר אספו את המזוודות, אבל שלכם לא יצאה. אתם ניגשים לדלפק שירותי המטען.

goal.en: Report the missing bag, describe it clearly, and find out how and when you'll get it back.
goal.he: לדווח על המזוודה החסרה, לתאר אותה בבירור ולברר איך ומתי תקבלו אותה בחזרה.

phrases.en: My suitcase didn't come out on the carousel.
phrases.he: המזוודה שלי לא יצאה על המסוע.

phrases.en: I think my bag might be lost.
Here's my bag tag. It's stuck to my boarding pass.
phrases.he: הנה מדבקת המזוודה. היא מודבקת על כרטיס העלייה למטוס.

phrases.en: It's a medium-sized dark blue suitcase with four wheels.
phrases.he: זו מזוודה בינונית, כחולה כהה, עם ארבעה גלגלים.
phrases.note: Adjective order: size, then colour, then the noun.

phrases.en: There's a red ribbon on the handle.
Could you deliver it to my hotel when it arrives?
phrases.he: אפשר לשלוח אותה למלון שלי כשהיא תגיע?

phrases.en: Is there a reference number so I can track it?
phrases.he: יש מספר פנייה, כדי שאוכל לעקוב אחרי המזוודה?

phrases.en: My medication is in that bag. What should I do?
phrases.he: התרופות שלי במזוודה הזאת. מה עושים?

phrases.en: Can I claim back the cost of a few essentials?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל החזר על כמה דברים בסיסיים שאקנה?
phrases.note: 'Essentials' = a toothbrush, a change of clothes and so on.

phrases.en: Where's baggage claim?
Where's baggage reclaim?
What a start to the trip! Thanks for your help, though.
phrases.he: איזו התחלה לטיול! אבל תודה על העזרה.

practice.partner: Hello, how can I help?

options.text: I didn't got my bag.

feedback.en: After 'didn't', use the base form: 'I didn't get my bag.'
feedback.he: אחרי didn't באה צורת הבסיס: I didn't get my bag.

options.text: Hi. I've just arrived from Tel Aviv, and my suitcase didn't come out on the carousel.

feedback.en: Clear and complete: where you came from and what happened. 'I've just arrived' (present perfect) fits perfectly.
feedback.he: ברור ומלא: מאיפה הגעתם ומה קרה. I've just arrived (present perfect) מתאים כאן בדיוק.

options.text: My bag is lost.

feedback.en: Understandable, but you don't know yet that it's lost. 'My bag didn't come out' is more accurate and less dramatic.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל עוד לא ידוע שהיא אבדה. My bag didn't come out מדויק יותר ופחות דרמטי.

model_replies: Hi. I've just arrived from Tel Aviv, and my suitcase didn't come out.
Hi, my bag didn't arrive on the flight from Frankfurt.

practice.partner: Can you describe the bag for me?

options.text: It's a medium-sized dark blue suitcase with four wheels and a red ribbon on the handle.

feedback.en: Size, colour and type, then one detail that makes it easy to spot: exactly what the agent needs.
feedback.he: גודל, צבע וסוג, ואז פרט אחד שעוזר לזהות אותה: בדיוק מה שהנציג צריך.

options.text: It's blue.

feedback.en: Far too little information: lots of bags are blue, so this won't help them find yours. Give the size, the type and something special about it.
feedback.he: מעט מדי מידע: הרבה מזוודות הן כחולות, וזה לא יעזור למצוא את שלכם. ציינו גודל, סוג ומשהו מיוחד בה.

options.text: It's a blue big suitcase with four wheels.

feedback.en: Useful details, but the adjective order is wrong: size comes before colour. Say 'a big blue suitcase'.
feedback.he: פרטים שימושיים, אבל סדר שמות התואר שגוי: גודל לפני צבע. אומרים a big blue suitcase.

model_replies: It's a medium-sized dark blue suitcase with four wheels.
It's a big black suitcase with a red ribbon on the handle.

practice.partner: It looks like it's still in Frankfurt. It should be on tomorrow morning's flight.

options.text: OK. I come back tomorrow to take it.

feedback.en: The idea works, but use 'will' for a decision: 'I'll come back tomorrow to pick it up.' It's also worth asking about delivery.
feedback.he: הרעיון עובד, אבל להחלטה משתמשים ב-will: I'll come back tomorrow to pick it up. כדאי גם לשאול על משלוח.

options.text: Tomorrow?! I need it now!

feedback.en: The frustration is understandable, but the agent can't make the bag fly faster. Ask what they can do for you tonight.
feedback.he: התסכול מובן, אבל הנציג לא יכול להטיס את המזוודה מהר יותר. עדיף לשאול במה אפשר לעזור הלילה.

options.text: That's a relief. Could you deliver it to my hotel, please?

feedback.en: You react naturally and ask for the most useful thing: delivery.
feedback.he: תגובה טבעית, ומבקשים את הדבר הכי שימושי: משלוח למלון.

model_replies: That's a relief. Could you deliver it to my hotel, please?
Great. Can you send it to my hotel when it arrives?

practice.partner: No problem. Can I have the address of your hotel?

options.text: Why you need my address?

feedback.en: A missing auxiliary: 'Why do you need my address?' And they need it so they can deliver your bag.
feedback.he: חסר פועל עזר: Why do you need my address? וחוץ מזה, הם צריכים את הכתובת כדי להביא לכם את המזוודה.

options.text: Sure, it's the Northern Hotel on Oxford Road.

feedback.en: Clear, with the name in the natural English order: 'the Northern Hotel'.
feedback.he: ברור, והשם בסדר הטבעי באנגלית: the Northern Hotel.

options.text: Hotel Northern, Oxford Road.

feedback.en: Understandable, but in English the name usually comes before 'Hotel', unlike in Hebrew. A full sentence also sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל באנגלית השם בא בדרך כלל לפני Hotel, בניגוד לעברית. משפט מלא גם נשמע נעים יותר.

model_replies: Sure, it's the Northern Hotel on Oxford Road.
It's the Northern Hotel. I'll write the address on the form.

practice.partner: Here's your reference number. You can track your bag online.

options.text: Great. One more thing: if I buy a few essentials tonight, can I claim the cost back?

feedback.en: A smart question to ask now, and 'claim back' is exactly the right verb.
feedback.he: שאלה חכמה לשאול כבר עכשיו, ו-claim back הוא בדיוק הפועל המתאים.

options.text: Thank you. Do you give money for clothes?

feedback.en: The idea comes across, but it sounds blunt. 'Can I claim back the cost of essentials?' is more precise.
feedback.he: הרעיון מובן, אבל זה נשמע בוטה. Can I claim back the cost of essentials? מדויק יותר.

options.text: OK, bye.

feedback.en: It sounds cold, and you miss the chance to ask about expenses. Thank the agent and ask what you need.
feedback.he: נשמע קר, ומפספסים את ההזדמנות לשאול על הוצאות. כדאי להודות ולשאול מה שצריך.

model_replies: Great. If I buy a few essentials tonight, can I claim the cost back?
Thanks. Should I keep my receipts for anything I buy?

roleplay.persona: Priya, a baggage services agent at Manchester Airport. Calm, kind and very organised; she has heard every lost-bag story and asks precise questions.
roleplay.complication: The system shows no trace of the bag at all, not in Frankfurt or anywhere else. Priya needs a detailed description and a list of what's inside, and she can't promise when it will turn up.
roleplay.opening_line: Hi there. Let me guess, your bag didn't turn up?

culture.en: Report a missing bag before you leave the baggage hall, and keep your bag tag and the reference number you're given.
culture.he: מדווחים על מזוודה חסרה לפני שיוצאים מאולם המזוודות, ושומרים את מדבקת המזוודה ואת מספר הפנייה שמקבלים.

culture.en: What airlines pay for while a bag is delayed varies. Keep every receipt and ask at the desk what they can cover.
culture.he: מה שחברות התעופה מכסות בזמן שמזוודה מתעכבת משתנה מחברה לחברה. שמרו כל קבלה ושאלו בדלפק מה אפשר לכסות.

variants.note: Americans mostly say 'fill out'; British speakers mostly say 'fill in'.
Both are common in the UK; 'Do you have...?' is standard in the US.

scenarios.title_en: Finding your gate for a connecting flight

situation.en: You've just landed at a big European airport. You have a connecting flight to Lisbon in two hours, but you don't know where to go. You ask at the information desk.
situation.he: נחתתם עכשיו בשדה תעופה גדול באירופה. בעוד שעתיים יש לכם טיסת המשך לליסבון, אבל אתם לא יודעים לאן ללכת. אתם שואלים בדלפק המידע.

goal.en: Ask where to go for your connecting flight and how to get to your gate, and understand simple directions.
goal.he: לשאול לאן הולכים לטיסת ההמשך ואיך מגיעים לשער, ולהבין הוראות הגעה פשוטות.

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is gate D7?
I have a connecting flight to Lisbon.
Where do I go for transfers?
Do I need to go through security again?
Is it far from here?
Sorry, could you say that again, more slowly?
phrases.he: סליחה, אפשר לחזור על זה לאט יותר?

phrases.en: So, left and then straight ahead?
Where's the restroom?
phrases.note: In the US, 'toilet' can sound a bit blunt; 'restroom' or 'bathroom' is more usual.

phrases.en: Where are the toilets?
Is there an elevator?
Is there a lift?
Thanks, have a good day!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Got it. Thank you so much!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: You're welcome. Have a good flight!

practice.partner: Hi, can I help you?

options.text: Lisbon. Where?

feedback.en: They'll probably understand you, but it's very short and sounds abrupt. A full sentence and 'please' are friendlier.
feedback.he: כנראה יבינו אתכם, אבל זה קצר מאוד ונשמע בוטה. משפט מלא ו-please נשמעים נעים יותר.

options.text: Yes. Where I go Lisbon?

feedback.en: Words are missing: 'do' and 'for'. Say 'Where do I go for the flight to Lisbon?'
feedback.he: חסרות מילים: do ו-for. אומרים: Where do I go for the flight to Lisbon?

options.text: Yes, please. I have a connecting flight to Lisbon. Where do I go?

feedback.en: Polite and clear: you say what you need and ask a direct question.
feedback.he: מנומס וברור: אומרים מה צריך ושואלים שאלה ישירה.

model_replies: Yes, please. I have a connecting flight to Lisbon. Where do I go?
Hi. Where do I go for my flight to Lisbon?

practice.partner: Your gate is D7. Follow the signs for Transfers.

options.text: I must security again?

feedback.en: A verb is missing. Say 'Do I need to go through security again?'
feedback.he: חסר פועל. אומרים: Do I need to go through security again?

options.text: Thank you. Do I need to go through security again?

feedback.en: A quick thank-you and a useful question.
feedback.he: תודה קצרה ושאלה שימושית.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but 'thank you' sounds friendlier, and it's a good moment to ask about security.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל thank you נשמע נעים יותר, וזה רגע טוב לשאול על הבידוק.

model_replies: Thank you. Do I need to go through security again?
Thanks! Is it far?

practice.partner: Go left, then straight ahead. It's about ten minutes on foot.

options.text: Sorry, could you say that again, more slowly?

feedback.en: Perfect when you didn't catch something. 'Sorry' plus 'could you' is polite and natural.
feedback.he: מושלם כשלא הבנתם. Sorry יחד עם could you: מנומס וטבעי.

options.text: What? Again.

feedback.en: 'What?' on its own can sound rude. 'Sorry?' or 'Pardon?' is softer.
feedback.he: What לבד יכול להישמע גס. Sorry? או Pardon? רכים יותר.

options.text: Speak slow!

feedback.en: This sounds like an order. Ask instead: 'Could you speak more slowly, please?'
feedback.he: זה נשמע כמו פקודה. עדיף לבקש: Could you speak more slowly, please?

model_replies: Sorry, could you say that again, more slowly?
So, left and then straight ahead? Thank you!

practice.partner: You'll see the D gates on your right. Have a good flight!

options.text: Yes, yes. Bye.

feedback.en: 'Yes, yes' sounds impatient, and you don't say thank you after someone has helped you. Say 'Thanks so much!'
feedback.he: Yes, yes נשמע חסר סבלנות, וגם לא אמרתם תודה למי שעזר לכם. אומרים: Thanks so much!

options.text: Thanks, you too!

feedback.en: Friendly, and people say this by mistake all the time! But 'you too' wishes them a good flight, and they aren't flying. 'Have a good day!' fits better.
feedback.he: חברותי, וזו טעות שקורה לכולם! אבל you too מאחל גם להם טיסה טובה, והם לא טסים. Have a good day! מתאים יותר.

options.text: Thanks so much. Have a good day!

feedback.en: Friendly and natural: you return the good wishes in a way that fits.
feedback.he: חברותי וטבעי: מחזירים איחול שמתאים למצב.

model_replies: Thanks so much. Have a good day!
Thank you! Bye!

roleplay.persona: Jonas, a friendly information desk worker at a big European airport. Speaks clearly, gives simple directions and is happy to repeat them.
roleplay.complication: The gate on the learner's boarding pass has changed from D7 to E2, which is further away, and boarding starts in 40 minutes. The learner needs to understand the new directions and ask how long it takes to get there.

culture.en: At big airports, follow the signs for 'Transfers' or 'Connecting flights', not 'Exit', if you have another flight.

scenarios.title_en: Your reservation can't be found

situation.en: It's 10 p.m. and you've just arrived at your hotel after a long day of travelling. You booked a double room for three nights through a booking website, but the receptionist can't find your reservation.
situation.he: השעה עשר בלילה, ואתם מגיעים למלון אחרי יום נסיעה ארוך. הזמנתם חדר זוגי לשלושה לילות דרך אתר הזמנות, אבל בקבלה לא מוצאים את ההזמנה.

goal.en: Stay calm, give details that help them find the booking, show your confirmation and agree on a solution for tonight.
goal.he: להישאר רגועים, למסור פרטים שיעזרו למצוא את ההזמנה, להציג את אישור ההזמנה ולהגיע לפתרון ללילה הזה.

phrases.en: Could you try searching by my email address?
phrases.he: אפשר לנסות לחפש לפי כתובת המייל שלי?

phrases.en: It might be spelled L-E-V-Y.
I booked it through a booking website about three weeks ago.

phrases.he: הנה מייל האישור עם מספר ההזמנה.

Is there any chance you have a room for tonight?

phrases.en: Would it be the same price as my booking?
I understand it's not your fault, but I really need somewhere to sleep tonight.

phrases.en: Could you contact the booking website to check?
phrases.he: אפשר ליצור קשר עם אתר ההזמנות ולבדוק?

phrases.en: No worries, these things happen.

feedback.en: Blaming someone else when the date is clearly wrong won't help. Accept it and look for a solution.
feedback.he: להאשים מישהו אחר כשהתאריך שגוי בבירור לא יעזור. עדיף לקבל את זה ולחפש פתרון.

options.text: Oh no, that's my mistake. Is there any chance you have a room for tonight?

feedback.en: Owning the mistake keeps the receptionist on your side, and 'Is there any chance...?' is a soft way to ask.

feedback.he: הטעות הייתה שלכם, ולכן לדרוש הנחה נשמע גס. אפשר לשאול בעדינות: Is there anything you can do on the price?

options.text: That could work. How much is it per night?

feedback.en: You're positive, but checking the price before you agree is sensible and perfectly polite.
feedback.he: מגיבים בחיוב, אבל בודקים את המחיר לפני שמסכימים. זה הגיוני ומנומס לגמרי.

options.text: OK, I'll take it.

feedback.en: Fine, but it's a good idea to ask the price before you say yes.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל כדאי לשאול על המחיר לפני שמסכימים.

model_replies: That sounds fine. How much is it per night?

feedback.en: You show you'll handle it, and you thank the receptionist for the extra effort.
feedback.he: מראים שתטפלו בזה בעצמכם, ומודים על המאמץ הנוסף.

options.text: Can't you do it for me?

feedback.en: You can ask, but the hotel may not be able to change a booking made on another website. Add 'please' and accept the answer.
feedback.he: אפשר לבקש, אבל ייתכן שהמלון לא יכול לשנות הזמנה שנעשתה באתר אחר. הוסיפו please וקבלו את התשובה.

options.text: OK, whatever.

feedback.en: 'Whatever' sounds dismissive and rude, especially after someone has helped you.
feedback.he: Whatever נשמע מזלזל וגס, במיוחד אחרי שעזרו לכם.

model_replies: No problem, I'll do it tonight. Thanks for your patience.

culture.he: כשמשהו משתבש, נימוס רגוע מביא באנגלית בדרך כלל תוצאות טובות יותר מכעס. I understand... ו-Is there any chance...? עוזרים מאוד.

goal.en: Check in and ask three simple questions: breakfast, the wifi password and checkout time.
goal.he: לעשות צ'ק-אין ולשאול שלוש שאלות פשוטות: על ארוחת הבוקר, על הסיסמה לוויי-פיי ועל שעת הצ'ק-אאוט.

goal.en: Describe both problems clearly and politely, and ask to move to a quieter room.

options.text: Hi, this is room 304. I'm afraid the air conditioning isn't working.

feedback.en: Room number first, then the problem. 'I'm afraid' softens bad news and sounds very natural in a complaint.
feedback.he: קודם מספר החדר, אחר כך הבעיה. I'm afraid מרכך בשורה רעה ונשמע טבעי מאוד בתלונה.

options.text: The air conditioning is broken.

feedback.en: Clear, but start with your room number so they know who's calling. A softener also sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל כדאי להתחיל במספר החדר כדי שיידעו מי מתקשר. מילה מרככת גם נשמעת נעים יותר.

model_replies: Hi, this is room 304. I'm afraid the air conditioning isn't working.
Hi, I'm calling from room 304. There's a problem with the AC.

practice.partner: I'm sorry about that. Have you tried the remote control?

options.text: Yes, I've tried it. It turns on, but it's only blowing warm air.

feedback.en: Present perfect for something that matters now, plus a precise description of the problem.
feedback.he: present perfect לפעולה שרלוונטית עכשיו, ותיאור מדויק של הבעיה.

options.text: Yes, of course I tried.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'of course' sounds a little impatient, as if the question were silly.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל of course נשמע קצת חסר סבלנות, כאילו השאלה מטופשת.

options.text: Yes, I tried, but it not working.

feedback.en: A verb is missing: 'it isn't working' or 'it's not working'.
feedback.he: חסר פועל: it isn't working או it's not working.

model_replies: Yes, I've tried it. It turns on, but it's only blowing warm air.
Yes, I've tried everything. Nothing happens.

practice.partner: I can send someone from maintenance to look at it in the morning.

options.text: In the morning? I want another room.

feedback.en: The request is reasonable, but 'I want' sounds demanding. Try 'Could I move to another room?'
feedback.he: הבקשה הגיונית, אבל I want נשמע תובעני. נסו: Could I move to another room?

options.text: Is not possible. Change me the room.

feedback.en: Ungrammatical, and it sounds like an order. Say 'Could I change rooms, please?' (note: rooms, plural).
feedback.he: לא תקין דקדוקית ונשמע כמו פקודה. אומרים: Could I change rooms, please? (שימו לב: rooms ברבים).

options.text: Thank you, but it's really hot tonight. Would it be possible to move to another room?

feedback.en: You thank them, explain why the morning is too late and politely ask for an alternative.
feedback.he: מודים, מסבירים למה הבוקר מאוחר מדי ומבקשים חלופה בנימוס.

model_replies: Thank you, but it's really hot tonight. Would it be possible to move to another room?
I appreciate that, but could I change rooms tonight instead?

practice.partner: Let me check... I have a room at the back on the fifth floor. It's a bit smaller, though.

options.text: I don't want small. I want big and quiet.

feedback.en: Sounds childish and demanding. If size matters, ask: 'Is there anything a bit bigger?'
feedback.he: נשמע ילדותי ותובעני. אם הגודל חשוב, שאלו: Is there anything a bit bigger?

options.text: That's fine, as long as it's quiet. Thank you.

feedback.en: 'As long as' sets your one condition clearly and politely.
feedback.he: as long as מציב את התנאי היחיד שלכם בצורה ברורה ומנומסת.

options.text: Smaller? Hmm, OK.

feedback.en: You agree, but you sound unhappy. If the size doesn't matter, say yes warmly.
feedback.he: אתם מסכימים, אבל נשמעים לא מרוצים. אם הגודל לא משנה לכם, הסכימו בחום.

model_replies: That's fine, as long as it's quiet. Thank you.
Perfect, a quiet room is all I need.

practice.partner: I'll send someone up with the new key in about ten minutes.

options.text: Great, thank you so much. I really appreciate it.

feedback.en: Warm thanks after a problem has been solved: exactly right.
feedback.he: תודה חמה אחרי שהבעיה נפתרה: בדיוק מה שצריך.

options.text: OK, ten minutes.

feedback.en: It confirms the time but sounds flat. A thank-you shows you appreciate the help.
feedback.he: מאשר את הזמן, אבל נשמע יבש. תודה מראה שאתם מעריכים את העזרה.

options.text: Ten minutes? Faster, please.

feedback.en: Ten minutes is reasonable. Pushing after they've solved your problem sounds rude.
feedback.he: עשר דקות זה סביר. ללחוץ אחרי שפתרו לכם את הבעיה נשמע גס.

model_replies: Great, thank you so much. I really appreciate it.
Perfect, thanks for sorting it out.

roleplay.persona: Javier, the evening receptionist at a busy city hotel in Barcelona. Friendly and apologetic, but the hotel is almost full tonight.
roleplay.complication: The only free room tonight is smaller and on the same noisy side of the building, just higher up; a quiet room will be free tomorrow. The learner has to negotiate, for example asking for a fan tonight, an earlier maintenance visit, or a guaranteed move in the morning.
roleplay.opening_line: Good evening, reception, Javier speaking. How can I help?

culture.en: Complain early and to the right person. Reception can usually fix much more on the first night than after you've checked out.
culture.he: כדאי להתלונן מוקדם ולאדם הנכון. בקבלה אפשר בדרך כלל לתקן הרבה יותר בלילה הראשון מאשר אחרי הצ'ק-אאוט.

culture.en: Complaints in English are usually softened: 'I'm afraid...', 'Would it be possible...?', 'I'd really appreciate it.' A direct demand can sound much ruder in English than it would in Hebrew.
culture.he: באנגלית נוהגים לרכך תלונות: I'm afraid..., Would it be possible...?, I'd really appreciate it. דרישה ישירה עלולה להישמע באנגלית הרבה יותר גסה מאשר בעברית.

variants.note: Informal short forms of 'air conditioning', which everyone understands.

scenarios.title_en: Extra towels and a late checkout

situation.en: You're staying at a hotel in Edinburgh. You need some extra towels, and on your last day your flight home isn't until the evening. You go down to reception.
situation.he: אתם מתארחים במלון באדינבורו. אתם צריכים עוד מגבות, וביום האחרון הטיסה הביתה רק בערב. אתם יורדים לקבלה.

goal.en: Ask for extra towels, then ask for a late checkout. If that isn't possible, arrange to leave your bags at the hotel.
goal.he: לבקש עוד מגבות, ואחר כך לבקש צ'ק-אאוט מאוחר. אם זה לא אפשרי, לסדר שתוכלו להשאיר את המזוודות במלון.

phrases.en: Could I have two extra towels, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל עוד שתי מגבות, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Could you send some more towels up to room 210?
Can I get another pillow?
phrases.note: 'Can I get...?' is very common in the US; 'Could I have...?' is safe everywhere.

phrases.en: Is it possible to have a late checkout tomorrow?
My flight isn't until 7 p.m.
Is there a charge for that?
Can I leave my luggage here after I check out?
phrases.he: אפשר להשאיר כאן את המזוודות אחרי הצ'ק-אאוט?

phrases.en: We've arrived early. Can we leave our bags until the room is ready?
phrases.he: הגענו מוקדם. אפשר להשאיר את המזוודות עד שהחדר יהיה מוכן?

phrases.en: Do you have luggage storage?
Could you keep our bags behind the desk for a few hours?
phrases.he: אפשר להשאיר אצלכם את התיקים לכמה שעות?

phrases.en: No worries if not.
phrases.note: Adding this makes a request feel low-pressure.

phrases.en: Perfect, that's really helpful.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi, could I have two extra towels for room 210, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. I'll have housekeeping bring them up in a few minutes.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thanks. Also, my flight home tomorrow isn't until 7 p.m. Is it possible to have a late checkout?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let me see... We're fully booked tomorrow, so the latest I can do is 12. Normal checkout is at 11.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: That would still help, thanks. Is there a charge for that?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No, that's fine. No charge.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. And after I check out, can I leave my luggage here until the afternoon?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yes, no problem. Just give your bags to the porter and you'll get a ticket.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. What time do I need to collect them by?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Any time before 9 p.m. Is there anything else I can help with?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No, that's everything. Thanks so much for your help.

practice.partner: Hi there, how can I help?

options.text: I need towels.

feedback.en: Clear, but blunt. Add 'Could I have...?' and your room number.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל בוטה. הוסיפו Could I have...? ואת מספר החדר.

options.text: Give me more towel.

feedback.en: It sounds like an order, and 'towel' needs to be plural: 'more towels'.
feedback.he: נשמע כמו פקודה, ו-towel צריך להיות ברבים: more towels.

options.text: Hi, could I have two extra towels for room 210, please?

feedback.en: Polite and complete: what you need, how many and where.
feedback.he: מנומס ומלא: מה צריך, כמה ולאיזה חדר.

model_replies: Hi, could I have two extra towels for room 210, please?
Hi, could you send some more towels up to room 210?

practice.partner: Of course. I'll have housekeeping bring them up. Anything else?

options.text: I will leave the room late tomorrow.

feedback.en: This sounds like you're informing them, not asking. A late checkout is a request: 'Is it possible to...?'
feedback.he: זה נשמע כמו הודעה ולא כמו בקשה. צ'ק-אאוט מאוחר מבקשים: Is it possible to...?

options.text: Yes, my flight tomorrow isn't until 7 p.m. Is it possible to have a late checkout?

feedback.en: Giving the reason first makes the request sound fair, and 'Is it possible...?' keeps it polite.
feedback.he: כשנותנים קודם סיבה, הבקשה נשמעת הוגנת, ו-Is it possible...? שומר על נימוס.

options.text: Can I stay in the room until 5 p.m. tomorrow?

feedback.en: A clear request, but asking for that long with no reason may get a quick 'no'. Explain why.
feedback.he: בקשה ברורה, אבל לבקש זמן ארוך כל כך בלי סיבה עלול להוביל ל'לא' מהיר. הסבירו למה.

model_replies: Yes, my flight isn't until 7 p.m. Is it possible to have a late checkout?
Could I possibly check out a bit later tomorrow? My flight's in the evening.

practice.partner: We're fully booked tomorrow, so the latest I can do is 12.

options.text: That would still help, thanks. Is there a charge for that?

feedback.en: You accept the compromise politely and check the cost before agreeing.
feedback.he: מקבלים את הפשרה בנימוס ובודקים את המחיר לפני שמסכימים.

options.text: Only 12? OK...

feedback.en: Understandable, but you sound disappointed, and they've already tried to help.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל אתם נשמעים מאוכזבים, וכבר ניסו לעזור לכם.

options.text: 12 is too early for me. I stay until 5.

feedback.en: Refusing and insisting sounds rude, and the room is booked. Ask about other options instead, like leaving your bags.
feedback.he: לסרב ולהתעקש נשמע גס, והחדר תפוס. עדיף לשאול על אפשרויות אחרות, כמו להשאיר את המזוודות.

model_replies: That would still help, thanks. Is there a charge for that?
OK, 12 is great. Thank you.

practice.partner: No charge. Can I help with anything else?

options.text: Where can I put my bags tomorrow?

feedback.en: Understandable, but less clear. Say that it's for after checkout.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל פחות ברור. ציינו שמדובר על אחרי הצ'ק-אאוט.

options.text: Can I forget my luggage here?

feedback.en: 'Forget' means leaving something by accident! When you leave something on purpose, the verb is 'leave': 'Can I leave my luggage here?'
feedback.he: forget פירושו לשכוח, כלומר להשאיר משהו בלי כוונה! כשמשאירים משהו בכוונה, הפועל הוא leave: Can I leave my luggage here?

options.text: Yes, can I leave my luggage here after I check out? I'll pick it up around 4.

feedback.en: Clear request, and saying when you'll be back helps them plan.
feedback.he: בקשה ברורה, וכשאומרים מתי תחזרו, קל להם להתארגן.

model_replies: Yes, can I leave my luggage here after I check out?
Do you have somewhere I can leave my bags until the afternoon?

practice.partner: Of course. Just give your bags to the porter, and you'll get a ticket.

options.text: Thank you for your helping.

feedback.en: Here you need the noun: 'Thank you for your help.'
feedback.he: כאן צריך את שם העצם: Thank you for your help.

options.text: Perfect, thanks so much for your help.

feedback.en: Warm and natural: a good way to finish.
feedback.he: חם וטבעי: דרך טובה לסיים.

options.text: OK. And the ticket is for what?

feedback.en: A fair question, but the word order is unnatural. Ask 'What's the ticket for?'
feedback.he: שאלה לגיטימית, אבל סדר המילים לא טבעי. שואלים: What's the ticket for?

model_replies: Perfect, thanks so much for your help.
Great, thank you!

roleplay.persona: Hamish, a receptionist at a traditional hotel in Edinburgh. Warm, chatty and a little formal, with a dry sense of humour.
roleplay.complication: Housekeeping has run out of clean bath towels for the next hour, and a late checkout is only possible for a fee. The learner should ask when the towels will come, how much the late checkout costs, and whether they can leave their bags instead.
roleplay.opening_line: Good afternoon! What can I do for you?

culture.en: In the US, guests usually tip the bellhop for carrying their bags, and many also tip housekeeping. In the UK, tipping hotel staff is appreciated but less expected.
culture.he: בארצות הברית נהוג לתת טיפ לסבל שמעלה את המזוודות, ורבים משאירים טיפ גם לצוות הניקיון. בבריטניה טיפ לצוות המלון מתקבל בברכה, אבל פחות מצופה.

culture.en: A late checkout is a favour, not a right. Asking the day before and giving a reason improves your chances.
culture.he: צ'ק-אאוט מאוחר הוא טובה ולא זכות. כשמבקשים יום לפני ונותנים סיבה, הסיכויים עולים.

variants.note: At stations and airports. In a hotel, both say 'luggage storage' or 'luggage room'.
The hotel worker who carries guests' bags.
Both are understood everywhere; 'collect' sounds more British.

scenarios.title_en: Checking out: querying a charge

situation.en: You're checking out of a hotel in San Francisco after four nights. On the bill you see two charges you don't remember: something from the minibar and a room-service dinner. (All prices here are made-up examples.)
situation.he: אתם עושים צ'ק-אאוט ממלון בסן פרנסיסקו אחרי ארבעה לילות. בחשבון מופיעים שני חיובים שאתם לא זוכרים: משהו מהמיני-בר וארוחת ערב משירות חדרים. (כל המחירים כאן הם דוגמה בלבד.)

goal.en: Query the charges firmly but politely, explain your side clearly, and get them removed or explained before you pay.
goal.he: לשאול על החיובים בנחישות אבל בנימוס, להסביר את הצד שלכם בבירור ולדאוג שיוסרו או יוסברו לפני התשלום.

phrases.en: Could I take a quick look at the bill before I pay?
phrases.he: אפשר לעבור רגע על החשבון לפני התשלום?

phrases.en: I think there might be a mistake on my bill.
phrases.he: נראה לי שאולי יש טעות בחשבון.

phrases.en: I don't recognize this charge. Could you tell me what it's for?
phrases.he: אני לא מזהה את החיוב הזה. אפשר לדעת על מה הוא?

phrases.en: We didn't use the minibar at all.
We didn't order room service. We ate out every night.
phrases.he: לא הזמנו שירות חדרים. אכלנו בחוץ כל ערב.

phrases.en: Could you check whether it was charged to the wrong room?
phrases.he: אפשר לבדוק אם זה חויב בטעות לחדר אחר?

phrases.en: Is there a signed receipt for that order?
phrases.he: יש קבלה חתומה על ההזמנה הזאת?

phrases.en: I'd like those charges removed, please.
phrases.note: Firm but polite. 'Remove these' on its own would sound rude.

phrases.en: I'm not comfortable paying for something we didn't have.
phrases.he: לא נוח לי לשלם על משהו שלא קיבלנו.

phrases.en: Could you email me the corrected bill?
phrases.he: אפשר לשלוח לי במייל את החשבון המתוקן?

phrases.en: Fair enough, that one's mine. Sorry!
phrases.he: מקובל עליי, את זה באמת לקחתי. סליחה!

phrases.en: Could I speak to a manager, please?
phrases.note: Use this only after you've tried to solve it with the person at the desk.

model_dialogue.text: Good morning! Checking out? Here's your bill. The total comes to $1,240.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thanks. Could I take a quick look before I pay?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course, take your time.

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hmm, the order says room 1412. You're in 1421, right? It looks like it was charged to the wrong room.

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: partner

model_dialogue.speaker: you
