practice.partner: Hi there. Where to?

options.text: Park View Hotel.

feedback.en: Drivers hear this a lot, so it works, but adding the street avoids confusion, and 'please' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: נהגים שומעים את זה הרבה, אז זה עובד, אבל הוספת הרחוב מונעת בלבול, ו-please נשמע ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?

feedback.en: Polite, and the street name helps the driver find it quickly.
feedback.he: מנומס, ושם הרחוב עוזר לנהג למצוא את המקום מהר.

options.text: I want to arrive to the Park View Hotel.

feedback.en: 'Arrive to' is wrong (it's 'arrive at'), and 'I want to arrive' sounds unnatural here. Say 'Could you take me to...?' or just 'The Park View Hotel, please.'
feedback.he: arrive to שגוי (אומרים arrive at), ו-I want to arrive לא טבעי כאן. אומרים Could you take me to...? או פשוט The Park View Hotel, please.

model_replies: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?
The Park View Hotel, please. It's on West 58th Street.

practice.partner: I can take the highway or go straight up through Midtown. The highway's longer, but there's less traffic. Your call.

options.text: Take the short way, and don't try to cheat me.

feedback.en: Accusing the driver of cheating is rude and may start an argument. If you're worried about the fare, just ask: 'Roughly how much will it be?'
feedback.he: להאשים את הנהג ברמאות זה גס ועלול להוביל לוויכוח. אם המחיר מדאיג אתכם, פשוט שואלים: Roughly how much will it be?

options.text: I don't know. You decide.

feedback.en: Acceptable, but it can sound a bit careless. 'Whichever's quicker is fine' gives the driver a clear instruction.
feedback.he: סביר, אבל עלול להישמע אדיש. Whichever's quicker is fine נותן לנהג הנחיה ברורה.

options.text: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?

feedback.en: Lets the driver choose but gives a clear priority, and checks the fare. 'Your call' means 'you decide'.
feedback.he: נותן לנהג לבחור אבל עם עדיפות ברורה, ובודק את המחיר. Your call פירושו 'ההחלטה שלך'.

model_replies: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?
Let's take the highway if it's faster. About how much will that be?

practice.partner: Sorry, I can't stop right outside the hotel. There's construction. Is the corner OK?

options.text: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.

feedback.en: Flexible and polite: you accept the change and thank the driver.
feedback.he: גמיש ומנומס: מקבלים את השינוי ומודים לנהג.

options.text: No, you must stop in front of the hotel.

feedback.en: 'You must' sounds like an order, and the driver may not be allowed to stop there. Accept it, or ask politely: 'Could you get any closer?'
feedback.he: You must נשמע כמו פקודה, ויכול להיות שלנהג אסור לעצור שם. אפשר להסכים, או לשאול בנימוס: Could you get any closer?

options.text: This is acceptable for me.

feedback.en: Understandable, but far too formal for a taxi. Say 'Sure, the corner's fine.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל רשמי מדי למונית. אומרים: Sure, the corner's fine.

model_replies: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.
No problem, the corner works. Thanks.

practice.partner: Here we are. That's twenty-eight fifty. Just tap your card on the screen back there.

options.text: Your machine is broken.

feedback.en: Clear, but it sounds like blame. 'The card machine doesn't seem to be working' is softer.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל נשמע מאשים. The card machine doesn't seem to be working רך יותר.

options.text: Sorry, I've tried twice, but the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?

feedback.en: 'Doesn't seem to be working' describes the problem politely without blaming anyone, and you ask for help.
feedback.he: doesn't seem to be working מתאר את הבעיה בנימוס בלי להאשים אף אחד, ומבקש עזרה.

options.text: The machine is broken, so I don't pay.

feedback.en: You still need to pay. Explain the problem and suggest another way: 'Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?'
feedback.he: עדיין צריך לשלם. מסבירים את הבעיה ומציעים דרך אחרת: Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?

model_replies: Sorry, I've tried twice, but the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?
Sorry, my card isn't going through. Could you restart the machine?

practice.partner: Sorry about that. It's still not working. Can you pay cash?

options.text: I have no cash. It's your problem.

feedback.en: Rude, and it doesn't solve anything. Suggest a solution: 'I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?'
feedback.he: גס, ולא פותר כלום. מציעים פתרון: I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?

options.text: Yes. Here.

feedback.en: It works, but it sounds abrupt. 'Sure, here you go' is friendlier.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל נשמע חד. Sure, here you go ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.

feedback.en: Natural: rounding up and saying 'Keep the change' is a simple way to tip in a US taxi. Here that's a tip of just over 20%.
feedback.he: טבעי: לעגל כלפי מעלה ולומר Keep the change היא דרך פשוטה להשאיר טיפ במונית בארצות הברית. כאן זה טיפ של קצת יותר מ-20%.

model_replies: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.
No problem, here you go. Keep the change.

roleplay.persona: Luis, a talkative New York taxi driver who has been driving for twenty years. He's friendly, proud of knowing every shortcut, talks quickly and likes chatting about the city and baseball.
roleplay.complication: Luis suggests a longer route that he says is 'faster at this time of day', and at the end the card reader in the back stops working, so the learner has to ask about other ways to pay.
roleplay.opening_line: Evening! Where are we headed?

culture.en: In New York, yellow cabs charge by the meter, and passengers usually add a tip, often around 15-20%. With rideshare apps the price is usually shown before you ride, and you can tip in the app.
culture.he: בניו יורק המוניות הצהובות גובות לפי מונה, ונוסעים בדרך כלל מוסיפים טיפ, לרוב בסביבות 15-20%. באפליקציות הסעות המחיר מוצג בדרך כלל מראש, ואפשר להוסיף טיפ באפליקציה.

culture.en: In London, you can stop a black cab in the street and it uses a meter, while a minicab has to be booked in advance. People often round up the fare instead of tipping a set percentage.
culture.he: בלונדון אפשר לעצור ברחוב מונית שחורה, והיא נוסעת לפי מונה, ואילו מיניקאב צריך להזמין מראש. נוהגים לעגל את הסכום כלפי מעלה במקום לתת טיפ באחוזים קבועים.

culture.en: Before getting into a rideshare, check the driver's name, the car and the plate number in the app. If they don't match, don't get in.
culture.he: לפני שנכנסים לרכב של אפליקציית הסעות, בודקים באפליקציה את שם הנהג, הרכב ומספר הרישוי. אם משהו לא תואם, לא נכנסים.

variants.note: A UK motorway is a major multi-lane road, like a US freeway or interstate.
'Taxi' is understood everywhere; 'cab' is more common in the US, and a London taxi is a 'black cab'.

scenarios.title_en: Metro and train: tickets, signs and announcements
scenarios.title_he: רכבת תחתית ורכבת: כרטיסים, שלטים והכרזות

situation.en: You're at Victoria station in London and need to get to King's Cross on the Underground. Later in the week you'll take a train to Brighton. You're not sure which ticket to buy, which line or platform to use, or what some announcements mean, so you ask a member of staff.
situation.he: אתם בתחנת ויקטוריה בלונדון וצריכים להגיע לקינגס קרוס ברכבת התחתית. בהמשך השבוע תיסעו ברכבת לברייטון. אתם לא בטוחים איזה כרטיס לקנות, באיזה קו או רציף להשתמש ומה אומרות חלק מההכרזות, ולכן אתם פונים לאחד מאנשי הצוות.

goal.en: Buy the right ticket (single or return), find the right line, direction and platform, and understand common signs and announcements.
goal.he: לקנות את הכרטיס המתאים (כיוון אחד או הלוך-חזור), למצוא את הקו, הכיוון והרציף הנכונים ולהבין שלטים והכרזות נפוצים.

scenarios.partner_role: station staff member / ticket office clerk

phrases.en: Excuse me, which line goes to King's Cross?
phrases.he: סליחה, איזה קו מגיע לקינגס קרוס?

phrases.en: Can I just use my bank card, or do I need a ticket?
phrases.he: אפשר פשוט להשתמש בכרטיס האשראי, או שצריך כרטיס נסיעה?
phrases.note: In London and many other cities you can tap a contactless card or phone at the gate.

phrases.en: A single to Brighton, please.
A one-way ticket to Boston, please.
A return to Brighton, please.
A round-trip ticket, please.
Which platform does it leave from?
Do I need to change trains?
How many stops is it?
Sorry, is this one going to King's Cross?
phrases.note: 'This one' = this train. Very common in quick questions on the platform.

phrases.en: Sorry, what did the announcement say?
Mind the gap.
phrases.note: A famous London Underground announcement and sign.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, could you help me? I need to get to King's Cross.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Have you got a contactless card or an Oyster card?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I've got a contactless bank card. Can I just use that?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yep. Just tap it on the yellow reader at the gate, and tap out again at the end of your journey.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. Which line do I need?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: The Victoria line, northbound. It's the light blue one on the map.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Do I need to change trains?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No, it's direct. Five stops, and King's Cross is the one after Euston.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK. Which way is the platform?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Follow the signs for the Victoria line, northbound. It's down the escalator.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. Thanks so much for your help!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No worries. And mind the gap!

practice.partner: Hi there, where are you travelling to today?

options.text: One ticket go and back to Brighton.

feedback.en: 'Go and back' is a word-for-word translation from Hebrew. Say 'a return' (UK) or 'a round-trip ticket' (US).
feedback.he: go and back הוא תרגום מילולי של 'הלוך-חזור'. אומרים a return (בריטניה) או a round-trip ticket (ארצות הברית).

options.text: Hi, a return to Brighton, please.

feedback.en: Short and natural. In the UK, 'a return' means a ticket there and back.
feedback.he: קצר וטבעי. בבריטניה a return פירושו כרטיס הלוך-חזור.

options.text: I want a ticket to Brighton and then back to London.

feedback.en: Understandable, but long and a bit direct. In the UK, just say 'A return to Brighton, please.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל ארוך וקצת ישיר מדי. בבריטניה פשוט אומרים A return to Brighton, please.

model_replies: Hi, a return to Brighton, please.
Could I have a return ticket to Brighton, please?

practice.partner: Are you coming back today or another day?

options.text: Today, this evening. Is there a cheaper ticket for that?

feedback.en: Answers clearly and asks a smart question: in the UK, ticket prices often depend on the day and time you travel.
feedback.he: עונה בבירור ושואל שאלה חכמה: בבריטניה מחיר הכרטיס תלוי לעיתים קרובות ביום ובשעה של הנסיעה.

options.text: I come back in the evening at today.

feedback.en: 'At today' is wrong; say 'this evening' or 'later today'. For a plan, use the present continuous: 'I'm coming back this evening.'
feedback.he: at today שגוי; אומרים this evening או later today. לתוכנית משתמשים בהווה מתמשך: I'm coming back this evening.

options.text: In the same day.

feedback.en: Almost: the preposition is 'on': 'On the same day.' Or simply: 'Today.'
feedback.he: כמעט: מילת היחס היא on: On the same day. או פשוט: Today.

model_replies: Today, this evening. Is there a cheaper ticket for that?
I'm coming back later today.

practice.partner: The next train's at 10:45 from platform 12.

options.text: Thank you very much.

feedback.en: Polite, but it's worth repeating the platform and time to check you heard them right.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל כדאי לחזור על הרציף והשעה כדי לוודא ששמעתם נכון.

options.text: What? Say again.

feedback.en: 'What?' sounds rude. To ask someone to repeat, say 'Sorry, could you say that again?' or 'Sorry, which platform?'
feedback.he: What? נשמע גס. כדי לבקש חזרה אומרים Sorry, could you say that again? או Sorry, which platform?

options.text: Platform 12 at 10:45. Thanks! Is it a direct train?

feedback.en: Repeating the key details is a smart way to check you heard correctly, and the follow-up question is useful.
feedback.he: חזרה על הפרטים החשובים היא דרך חכמה לוודא ששמעתם נכון, ושאלת ההמשך שימושית.

model_replies: Platform 12 at 10:45. Thanks! Is it a direct train?
Sorry, was that platform 12? Thanks.

practice.partner: I'm afraid the Victoria line is suspended this morning, so you'll need to take a bus or go a different way.

options.text: Oh, OK. What's the best way to get to King's Cross, then?

feedback.en: Accepts the change and immediately asks for the information you need.
feedback.he: מקבל את השינוי ומיד שואל את מה שצריך לדעת.

options.text: What means 'suspended'?

feedback.en: Asking about a new word is a good idea, but the question needs 'does': 'What does suspended mean?' Here it means the line isn't running for now.
feedback.he: לשאול על מילה חדשה זה רעיון טוב, אבל בשאלה צריך does: What does suspended mean? כאן הכוונה שהקו לא פועל כרגע.

options.text: OK. Where is the bus?

feedback.en: Understandable, but vague: there are many buses. Ask which one: 'Which bus goes to King's Cross?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל כללי מדי: יש הרבה אוטובוסים. שואלים איזה: Which bus goes to King's Cross?

model_replies: Oh, OK. What's the best way to get to King's Cross, then?
Oh no. Which bus goes to King's Cross from here?

practice.partner: You can just tap your bank card or phone on the yellow reader. Where are you heading?

options.text: OK, I tap. I go to King's Cross.

feedback.en: Understandable, but use 'I'll' for a decision you make now and 'I'm going' for where you're headed: 'OK, I'll tap. I'm going to King's Cross.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל להחלטה של הרגע משתמשים ב-I'll, ולתיאור לאן נוסעים ב-I'm going: OK, I'll tap. I'm going to King's Cross.

options.text: Great, thanks. I'm going to King's Cross. Is it northbound?

feedback.en: Natural and useful: Tube platforms are signed by direction (northbound, southbound, eastbound, westbound), so checking the direction helps you get on the right train.
feedback.he: טבעי ושימושי: הרציפים ברכבת התחתית של לונדון מסומנים לפי כיוון (northbound, southbound, eastbound, westbound), ולכן כדאי לבדוק את הכיוון כדי לעלות לרכבת הנכונה.

options.text: Where is subway to King's Cross?

feedback.en: Two problems: it needs 'the', and in London the trains are 'the Underground' or 'the Tube'. In British English a 'subway' is usually a tunnel for walking under a road, so this can confuse people. Ask: 'Which line goes to King's Cross?'
feedback.he: שתי בעיות: חסר the, ובלונדון הרכבת התחתית נקראת the Underground או the Tube. באנגלית בריטית subway הוא בדרך כלל מעבר תת-קרקעי להולכי רגל מתחת לכביש, ולכן זה עלול לבלבל. שואלים: Which line goes to King's Cross?

model_replies: Great, thanks. I'm going to King's Cross. Is it northbound?
Thanks! I'm heading to King's Cross. Which line do I need?

roleplay.persona: Gemma, a patient member of staff at a busy London Underground station. She speaks clearly, uses typical British transport words (single, return, platform, 'change at...') and is helpful, though she's dealing with lots of passengers.
roleplay.complication: The line the learner planned to take has a problem today, so Gemma suggests a different route with one change. The learner must check the new line, the direction and where to change, and ask her to repeat anything they miss.
roleplay.opening_line: Morning! You look a bit lost. Where are you trying to get to?

culture.en: On London Underground escalators, people stand on the right and walk on the left. Standing on the left is a classic visitor mistake.
culture.he: במדרגות הנעות ברכבת התחתית של לונדון עומדים בצד ימין והולכים בצד שמאל. לעמוד בצד שמאל היא טעות קלאסית של תיירים.

culture.en: In London and New York you can usually tap a contactless bank card or phone at the gate instead of buying a paper ticket. Fares and rules change, so check the official transport website before you travel.
culture.he: בלונדון ובניו יורק אפשר בדרך כלל להצמיד כרטיס אשראי ללא מגע או טלפון בשער, במקום לקנות כרטיס נייר. המחירים והכללים משתנים, ולכן כדאי לבדוק באתר הרשמי של התחבורה הציבורית לפני הנסיעה.

culture.en: Announcements are often fast and hard to hear. It's completely normal to ask someone nearby: 'Sorry, what did they just say?'
culture.he: ההכרזות לעיתים קרובות מהירות וקשות לשמיעה. זה נורמלי לגמרי לשאול מישהו לידכם: Sorry, what did they just say?

variants.note: 'Metro' is understood in both and is the usual word in many other cities.
Many US stations say 'track 9' where British stations say 'platform 9'; 'platform' is understood in both.

variants.us: Stand clear of the closing doors.
variants.note: Typical announcements before the doors close.

scenarios.title_en: Renting a car: licence, insurance, fuel and damage
scenarios.title_he: השכרת רכב: רישיון, ביטוח, דלק ונזקים

situation.en: You're picking up a rental car at Edinburgh Airport for a week in the Scottish Highlands. The agent checks your licence, offers extra insurance and explains the fuel policy. When you inspect the car, you notice a scratch that isn't on the damage form. A week later, at the return desk, there's a disagreement about a dent.
situation.he: אתם אוספים רכב שכור בשדה התעופה של אדינבורו לשבוע בהיילנדס הסקוטיים. הנציגה בודקת את הרישיון, מציעה ביטוח נוסף ומסבירה את מדיניות הדלק. כשאתם בודקים את הרכב, אתם מגלים שריטה שלא מופיעה בטופס הנזקים. שבוע אחר כך, בהחזרת הרכב, מתגלעת מחלוקת על מכה בדלת.

goal.en: Confirm your booking and documents, understand what the insurance covers before agreeing to extras, check the fuel policy, get existing damage recorded and handle a damage dispute calmly.
goal.he: לאשר את ההזמנה והמסמכים, להבין מה הביטוח מכסה לפני שמסכימים לתוספות, לברר את מדיניות הדלק, לוודא שנזק קיים נרשם ולהתמודד ברוגע עם מחלוקת על נזק.

phrases.en: Hi, I've got a booking under the name Cohen.
phrases.he: היי, יש לי הזמנה על שם כהן.
phrases.note: 'Booking' is more common in the UK, 'reservation' in the US; both are understood.

phrases.en: Here's my driving licence and passport.
phrases.note: US: 'driver's license'.

phrases.en: Do I need an international driving permit?
What exactly does the basic insurance cover?
What's the excess if something happens?
phrases.he: מה גובה ההשתתפות העצמית אם קורה משהו?

phrases.en: What's the deductible on the basic coverage?
I think I'll stick with the basic cover, thanks.
phrases.he: נראה לי שאסתפק בכיסוי הבסיסי, תודה.

phrases.en: Is it full to full?
phrases.note: Full to full: you get the car with a full tank and bring it back full.

phrases.en: Does it take petrol or diesel?
phrases.he: הוא על בנזין או על סולר?
phrases.note: US: 'gas or diesel'.

phrases.en: Is it a manual or an automatic?
There's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't marked on the form.
phrases.he: יש שריטה על הפגוש האחורי שלא מסומנת בטופס.

phrases.en: Could you note that down, please? I'd like it on record.
phrases.he: אפשר לרשום את זה, בבקשה? חשוב לי שזה יתועד.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hiya, welcome to Edinburgh. Have you got a booking with us?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, it's under the name Cohen. Here's my driving licence and passport.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Lovely, thanks. So that's a compact car for seven days. Would you like to add our premium cover? It reduces your excess to zero.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: What's the excess with the basic insurance?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: With basic cover, you'd pay the first thousand pounds of any damage.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I see. And how much is the premium cover?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's an extra fifteen pounds a day.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I think I'll stick with the basic cover, thanks. What's the fuel policy?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's full to full, so please bring it back with a full tank, or there's a refuelling charge.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Got it. Oh, and before I drive off: there's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't on the form.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Thanks for pointing that out. I'll come and have a look and add it to the damage report.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. Could I have a copy of the updated form, please?

practice.partner: Can I see your driving licence, please? And will anyone else be driving?

options.text: Here. Why do you need to know?

feedback.en: This sounds suspicious and defensive. Agents ask because extra drivers usually have to be added to the rental agreement.
feedback.he: נשמע חשדני ומתגונן. שואלים כי נהגים נוספים צריכים בדרך כלל להירשם בחוזה ההשכרה.

options.text: Sure, here you go. No, it'll just be me.

feedback.en: Natural and complete: you hand over the document and answer the question clearly.
feedback.he: טבעי ומלא: מוסרים את המסמך ועונים על השאלה בבירור.

options.text: Yes, here. Only I drive.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'Only I drive' sounds like a general habit. For this rental, say 'It'll just be me' or 'I'll be the only driver'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל Only I drive נשמע כמו הרגל כללי. לגבי ההשכרה הזאת אומרים It'll just be me או I'll be the only driver.

model_replies: Sure, here you go. No, it'll just be me.
Here you are. I'll be the only driver.

practice.partner: I'd really recommend our premium cover. Without it, you'd pay the first £1,200 of any damage.

options.text: Thanks. Before I decide, could you tell me exactly what it covers? Are the tyres and windscreen included?

feedback.en: Asks for details before agreeing, which is exactly right with insurance. 'Tyres' and 'windscreen' are the British words (US: tires, windshield).
feedback.he: מבקש פרטים לפני שמסכימים, וזה בדיוק מה שצריך לעשות עם ביטוח. tyres ו-windscreen הן המילים הבריטיות (בארצות הברית: tires, windshield).

options.text: No thanks, I don't need it.

feedback.en: A clear, acceptable answer, but you're accepting a big risk without asking a single question. It's worth checking what's covered first.
feedback.he: תשובה ברורה ולגיטימית, אבל אתם לוקחים על עצמכם סיכון גדול בלי לשאול אף שאלה. כדאי לבדוק קודם מה הכיסוי כולל.

options.text: I don't want your insurance. You just want my money.

feedback.en: Accusing the agent is rude. Agents are often expected to offer extras; a calm 'No, thank you' or a clear question works much better.
feedback.he: להאשים את הנציגה זה גס. נציגים נדרשים לעיתים קרובות להציע תוספות; No, thank you רגוע או שאלה ברורה עובדים הרבה יותר טוב.

model_replies: Thanks. Before I decide, could you tell me exactly what it covers? Are the tyres and windscreen included?
What exactly does it cover that the basic insurance doesn't?

practice.partner: It's full to full on this one. Any questions about the fuel?

options.text: What is full to full? I don't understand nothing.

feedback.en: Double negative: say 'I don't understand anything', or better, 'Sorry, what does full to full mean?'
feedback.he: שלילה כפולה: אומרים I don't understand anything, ועוד יותר טוב: Sorry, what does full to full mean?

options.text: Just one: does it take petrol or diesel? And is there a petrol station near the airport for when I bring it back?

feedback.en: Two practical questions that prevent expensive mistakes, like putting the wrong fuel in the car.
feedback.he: שתי שאלות מעשיות שמונעות טעויות יקרות, כמו תדלוק בדלק הלא נכון.

options.text: So I bring it full?

feedback.en: Statement questions are common in speech, but you need 'back': 'So I bring it back full?' It's also worth asking about petrol or diesel.
feedback.he: שאלה בצורת משפט חיווי נפוצה בדיבור, אבל חסר back: So I bring it back full? וכדאי לשאול גם אם הרכב על בנזין או על סולר.

model_replies: Just one: does it take petrol or diesel? And is there a petrol station near the airport?
So I need to bring it back with a full tank. Is it petrol or diesel?

practice.partner: Right, you're all set. Just sign here to confirm there's no damage apart from what's on the form.

options.text: Wait. I need to check the car first.

feedback.en: The right idea, but 'Wait' and 'I need to' sound a little sharp. 'Could I check the car first?' gets the same result more politely.
feedback.he: הרעיון נכון, אבל Wait ו-I need to נשמעים קצת חדים. Could I check the car first? משיג את אותו הדבר בנימוס.

options.text: Sure, the car is perfect, I'll sign.

feedback.en: Polite, but risky: you're confirming the car has no other damage without looking. Always check, and take photos, before you sign.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל מסוכן: אתם מאשרים שאין נזק נוסף בלי להסתכל. תמיד בודקים ומצלמים לפני שחותמים.

options.text: Could I check the car before I sign? I'd just like to make sure everything's on the form.

feedback.en: Sensible and polite: you only sign after checking, and the reason sounds reasonable, not suspicious.
feedback.he: נבון ומנומס: חותמים רק אחרי בדיקה, וההסבר נשמע סביר ולא חשדני.

model_replies: Could I check the car before I sign? I'd just like to make sure everything's on the form.
Would you mind if I had a quick look at the car before I sign?

practice.partner: Is everything OK with the car?

options.text: Mostly, yes, but there's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't on the form. Could you add it, please?

feedback.en: Says exactly where the damage is and what you want done about it.
feedback.he: אומר בדיוק איפה הנזק ומה אתם מבקשים לעשות.

options.text: Somebody broke your car.

feedback.en: 'Broke' is far too strong for a scratch and sounds dramatic. Describe it exactly: 'There's a small scratch on the rear bumper.'
feedback.he: broke חזק מדי לשריטה ונשמע דרמטי. מתארים בדיוק: There's a small scratch on the rear bumper.

options.text: There is a scratch here.

feedback.en: Clear, but add where it is and what you'd like: 'Could you add it to the form, please?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל כדאי להוסיף איפה בדיוק ומה אתם מבקשים: Could you add it to the form, please?

model_replies: Mostly, yes, but there's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't on the form. Could you add it, please?
Almost. There's a small scratch here that isn't marked. Could you note it down?

practice.partner: We've found a dent on the passenger door, I'm afraid. We'll have to charge it to your card.

options.text: That's not my fault. It was there before.

feedback.en: Your point is clear, but it sounds defensive and gives no evidence. Mention the form or your photos.
feedback.he: הטענה ברורה, אבל נשמעת מתגוננת ואין בה ראיות. הזכירו את הטופס או את התמונות.

options.text: I'm sorry, but that dent was already there when I picked the car up. It's on the damage form, and I've got photos from the pick-up too.

feedback.en: Calm, firm and backed by evidence: exactly how to handle a dispute. 'I'm sorry, but...' signals polite disagreement.
feedback.he: רגוע, נחוש ומגובה בראיות: בדיוק כך מתמודדים עם מחלוקת. I'm sorry, but... מסמן אי-הסכמה מנומסת.

options.text: No way, I'm not paying anything. You're lying!

feedback.en: Calling the agent a liar escalates the situation. Stay calm, show your proof and, if needed, ask to speak to a manager.
feedback.he: לקרוא לנציגה שקרנית רק מסלים את המצב. נשארים רגועים, מציגים הוכחות, ואם צריך מבקשים לדבר עם מנהל.

model_replies: I'm sorry, but that dent was already there when I picked the car up. It's on the damage form, and I've got photos too.
I don't think that's right. The dent is marked on the pick-up form. Could we look at it together?

roleplay.persona: Fiona, a professional and slightly sales-focused rental agent at Edinburgh Airport. She's polite and efficient, speaks with a light Scottish accent ('Hiya', 'wee'), and is expected to sell extra insurance, so she'll recommend it more than once.
roleplay.complication: Fiona pushes the premium insurance and a paid upgrade, and the damage form she hands over is missing a scratch that's clearly visible on the car. The learner must ask clear questions, politely decline what they don't want and get the damage recorded before driving away.
roleplay.opening_line: Hiya, welcome to Edinburgh! Have you got a booking with us today?

culture.en: In the UK and Ireland, people drive on the left, and many rental cars are manual. If you can only drive an automatic, ask for one when you book.
culture.he: בבריטניה ובאירלנד נוהגים בצד שמאל של הכביש, ורכבים שכורים רבים הם ידניים. אם אתם נוהגים רק באוטומט, בקשו זאת כבר בהזמנה.

culture.en: Walk around the car and take photos or a short video before you leave and again when you return it. It's your best evidence if there's a disagreement about damage.
culture.he: הקיפו את הרכב וצלמו תמונות או סרטון קצר לפני היציאה ושוב בהחזרה. זו הראיה הכי טובה שלכם אם תהיה מחלוקת על נזק.

culture.en: Minimum age, international driving permits, deposits and insurance rules vary by company and country, so read the rental terms before you travel.
culture.he: גיל מינימלי, רישיון נהיגה בינלאומי, פיקדונות וכללי ביטוח משתנים בין חברות ומדינות, ולכן כדאי לקרוא את תנאי ההשכרה לפני הנסיעה.

variants.note: Both are understood in both countries.

scenarios.title_en: Asking for directions on the street

situation.en: You're walking around a city centre and can't find the City Museum, and your phone's battery is dead. You stop someone on the street to ask for directions.
situation.he: אתם מסתובבים במרכז העיר ולא מוצאים את מוזיאון העיר, והסוללה בטלפון נגמרה. אתם עוצרים מישהו ברחוב ושואלים איך מגיעים.

goal.en: Stop a stranger politely, ask how to get to a place, understand simple directions and say thank you.
goal.he: לעצור אדם זר בנימוס, לשאול איך מגיעים למקום מסוים, להבין הוראות פשוטות ולהודות.

phrases.en: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.
Excuse me, where's the museum?
How do I get to the train station?
Is it far?
Can I walk there?
Go straight on.
phrases.note: US: 'Go straight ahead' or 'Keep going straight'.

phrases.en: Turn left at the traffic lights.
phrases.note: In the US people often say 'at the light'.

phrases.en: Take the second right.
It's on your left.
Go two blocks and turn right.
phrases.note: 'Block' is very common in the US, where many streets form a grid.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?
phrases.he: סליחה, אפשר לחזור על זה לאט יותר?

phrases.en: Great, thanks a lot!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, sorry. Where's the City Museum?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: The City Museum? It's not far. About ten minutes on foot.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. How do I get there?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Go straight on, then turn left at the traffic lights.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Left at the traffic lights. OK.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Then take the second right. The museum's on your left, next to a big park.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Straight on, left at the lights, then the second right. It's on the left.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thank you so much!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No problem. Enjoy the museum!

practice.partner: Yes? Can I help you?

options.text: Museum! Where?

feedback.en: Too short, and it sounds like an order. Ask a full, polite question: 'Where's the museum, please?'
feedback.he: קצר מדי ונשמע כמו פקודה. שואלים שאלה מלאה ומנומסת: Where's the museum, please?

options.text: I search the museum.

feedback.en: Understandable, but say 'I'm looking for the museum.' 'Search' means to look carefully through something, like a bag.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל אומרים I'm looking for the museum. המשמעות של search היא לחפש בתוך משהו, למשל בתיק.

options.text: Yes, please. Where's the City Museum?

feedback.en: Short, polite and clear. Perfect.
feedback.he: קצר, מנומס וברור. מושלם.

model_replies: Yes, please. Where's the City Museum?
Yes, please. I'm looking for the City Museum.

practice.partner: Oh, it's quite far. About thirty minutes on foot.

options.text: Oh, OK. Is there a bus?

feedback.en: A natural reaction and a useful question.
feedback.he: תגובה טבעית ושאלה שימושית.

options.text: It is far. I go with bus?

feedback.en: Understood, but we 'take' a bus or go 'by bus', not 'with bus': 'Can I take a bus?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל באנגלית take a bus או by bus, לא with bus: Can I take a bus?

options.text: Why is it so far?

feedback.en: This sounds strange: the person can't change the distance! Ask about another way to get there.
feedback.he: נשמע מוזר: האדם לא יכול לשנות את המרחק! שואלים על דרך אחרת להגיע.

model_replies: Oh, OK. Is there a bus?
Oh, that's far. Can I take a bus?

practice.partner: Go straight on, then turn right at the traffic lights.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but repeating the directions ('Right at the lights?') is a good way to check.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל חזרה על ההוראות (Right at the lights?) היא דרך טובה לוודא שהבנתם.

options.text: Straight on, then right at the lights. Thank you!

feedback.en: Repeating the directions helps you remember and lets the person correct you if needed.
feedback.he: חזרה על ההוראות עוזרת לזכור ומאפשרת לאדם לתקן אתכם אם צריך.

options.text: What? I don't understand you.

feedback.en: 'What?' sounds rude, and 'I don't understand you' can sound like criticism. Say 'Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?'
feedback.he: What? נשמע גס, ו-I don't understand you עלול להישמע כמו ביקורת. אומרים Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?

model_replies: Straight on, then right at the lights. Thank you!
So, straight on and right at the traffic lights? Thanks!

practice.partner: Sorry, I'm not from here. I don't know.

options.text: You don't know? Really?

feedback.en: This sounds surprised and a bit rude. Lots of people in a city are visitors too.
feedback.he: נשמע מופתע וקצת גס. גם הרבה אנשים אחרים בעיר הם תיירים.

options.text: No problem, thanks anyway!

feedback.en: 'Thanks anyway' is the perfect phrase when someone tries to help but can't.
feedback.he: Thanks anyway הוא הביטוי המושלם כשמישהו מנסה לעזור אבל לא יכול.

options.text: OK, thank you.

feedback.en: Polite and fine. 'Thanks anyway' is a little more natural here.
feedback.he: מנומס ובסדר. Thanks anyway טבעי קצת יותר כאן.

model_replies: No problem, thanks anyway!
Oh, OK. Thanks anyway!

practice.partner: It's just over there, opposite the bank. You can't miss it!

options.text: Oh, I see it! Thanks so much.

feedback.en: Natural and warm. 'You can't miss it' just means it's easy to find.
feedback.he: טבעי וחם. You can't miss it פירושו פשוט שקל מאוד למצוא את המקום.

options.text: I can't to miss it.

feedback.en: After 'can' we don't use 'to': 'I can't miss it.' But you don't need to repeat this phrase; it just means the place is easy to find. Just say thanks!
feedback.he: אחרי can לא באה to: I can't miss it. אבל אין צורך לחזור על הביטוי; הוא רק אומר שקל למצוא את המקום. פשוט אומרים תודה!

options.text: Thank you very much for your help. I am very grateful.

feedback.en: Polite, but very formal for a quick question on the street. 'Thanks so much!' sounds more natural.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל רשמי מאוד לשאלה קצרה ברחוב. Thanks so much! נשמע טבעי יותר.

model_replies: Oh, I see it! Thanks so much.
Great, thanks a lot!

roleplay.persona: Margaret, a kind retired teacher in her sixties who is walking her dog. She's happy to help and speaks clearly, but gives directions full of local landmarks ('past the old church, by the bakery').
roleplay.complication: Margaret first sends the learner the wrong way by mistake, then corrects herself ('Oh no, sorry, I meant left!'). The learner must check and repeat the directions to be sure.
roleplay.opening_line: Hello there, are you all right? You look a bit lost.

culture.en: Start with 'Excuse me' to get a stranger's attention, and add 'sorry' if they're busy. It's expected, especially in the UK, and people are usually happy to help.
culture.he: פותחים ב-Excuse me כדי למשוך את תשומת הלב של אדם זר, ומוסיפים sorry אם הוא עסוק. זה מצופה, במיוחד בבריטניה, ואנשים בדרך כלל שמחים לעזור.

culture.en: In the US, directions often use blocks ('Go two blocks north'), because many city centres are built on a grid. In the UK, people tend to use landmarks ('Go past the church; it's opposite the bank').
culture.he: בארצות הברית נותנים הוראות בעזרת blocks (Go two blocks north), כי מרכזי ערים רבים בנויים ברשת של רחובות. בבריטניה נוטים להיעזר בציוני דרך (Go past the church; it's opposite the bank).

scenarios.title_en: Trying on clothes: sizes and colours

situation.en: You're in a clothes shop in London. You've found a jacket you really like, but it's the wrong size, and you'd like to see it in another colour.
situation.he: אתם בחנות בגדים בלונדון. מצאתם ז'קט שממש מוצא חן בעיניכם, אבל המידה לא מתאימה, ואתם רוצים לראות אותו גם בצבע אחר.

goal.en: Ask for your size and another colour, try the jacket on, say how it fits and decide what to buy.
goal.he: לבקש את המידה שלכם וצבע אחר, למדוד את הז'קט, להגיד איך הוא יושב עליכם ולהחליט מה קונים.

phrases.en: Excuse me, do you have this in a medium?
phrases.he: סליחה, יש לכם את זה במידה M?
phrases.note: Clothing sizes are usually said as words: small, medium, large.

phrases.en: Does this come in any other colours?
Have you got this in a smaller size?
phrases.he: יש לכם את זה במידה קטנה יותר?
phrases.note: 'Have you got…?' is very British. 'Do you have…?' works everywhere.

phrases.en: Could I try this on, please?
phrases.note: 'Try on' = put clothes on to see if they fit. Don't say 'measure'.

phrases.en: Where are the fitting rooms?
phrases.note: Also 'changing rooms' (UK) or 'dressing rooms' (US).

phrases.en: It's a bit tight around the shoulders.
phrases.note: For clothes, 'tight' (not 'narrow') is the opposite of 'loose'.

phrases.en: It's a bit big. Do you have the next size down?
phrases.he: זה קצת גדול. יש לכם מידה אחת קטנה יותר?

phrases.en: Does it run small?
phrases.note: 'Run small/large' = the sizes are smaller or bigger than usual.

phrases.en: Do these trousers come in black?
phrases.note: In the UK, 'pants' means underwear, so say 'trousers'.

phrases.en: Do these pants come in black?
phrases.note: In the US, 'pants' are trousers.

phrases.en: I'm just looking, thanks.
phrases.note: The standard answer when you don't need help yet.

phrases.en: Perfect, I'll take it!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi there! Are you looking for anything in particular?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let me check… Yes, here you go. That's the last medium in navy.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thanks. Does it come in any other colours?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: We've got it in black and olive green as well.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Ooh, could I try the black one too, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. The changing rooms are at the back, on the left.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: So, how did they fit?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight around the shoulders.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yeah, that one runs a bit small. Shall I get you the navy in a large?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Lovely. You can pay at the till whenever you're ready.

practice.partner: Hi there! Are you looking for anything in particular?

options.text: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?

feedback.en: Natural and specific: you say yes and ask for exactly what you need.
feedback.he: טבעי וממוקד: עונים בחיוב ומבקשים בדיוק את מה שצריך.

options.text: I search a jacket in medium size.

feedback.en: Two problems: the verb is 'look for', not 'search', and for something you're doing right now we use the present continuous: 'I'm looking for a jacket in a medium.'
feedback.he: שתי בעיות: הפועל הוא look for ולא search, ועל משהו שעושים ממש עכשיו משתמשים בהווה מתמשך: I'm looking for a jacket in a medium.

options.text: Yes. I need this jacket, size medium.

feedback.en: Clear, but 'I need' sounds a bit like an order. A question ('Have you got…?') is friendlier.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל I need נשמע קצת כמו הוראה. שאלה כמו Have you got...? נעימה יותר.

model_replies: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?
Yes, please. Do you have this in a medium?

practice.partner: We've got it in black and olive green as well.

options.text: Black.

feedback.en: Understandable, but one word can sound cold. Add 'Could I see…' or 'please'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל מילה אחת עלולה להישמע קרה. כדאי להוסיף Could I see... או please.

options.text: Can I measure the black one?

feedback.en: 'Measure' means checking size with a tape measure. When you put clothes on to check them, it's 'try on'.
feedback.he: measure פירושו למדוד עם סרט מדידה. כשלובשים בגד כדי לבדוק אותו אומרים try on.

options.text: Ooh, could I try the black one too, please?

feedback.en: Polite and natural. 'The black one' saves you repeating 'jacket'.
feedback.he: מנומס וטבעי. the black one חוסך את החזרה על המילה jacket.

model_replies: Could I try the black one too, please?
Oh nice. Can I try it on in black as well?

practice.partner: The changing rooms are at the back. How many items have you got?

options.text: Just two, thanks.

feedback.en: Short, friendly and exactly what they asked.
feedback.he: קצר, נעים ובדיוק מה ששאלו.

options.text: Why you need to know?

feedback.en: The question needs 'do' ('Why do you need to know?'), and it sounds suspicious. Many shops count items before you try them on; it's routine.
feedback.he: חסר do בשאלה (Why do you need to know?), וזה גם נשמע חשדני. חנויות רבות סופרות פריטים לפני מדידה, זה עניין שגרתי.

options.text: I have two items: the navy jacket and the black jacket.

feedback.en: Correct, but more detail than needed. A number is enough.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל יותר פרטים ממה שצריך. מספיק להגיד מספר.

model_replies: Just two, thanks.
Two, thanks.

practice.partner: So, how did they fit?

options.text: The navy one is very narrow on me.

feedback.en: 'Narrow' describes width, like a narrow street. For clothes that are too small, say 'tight'.
feedback.he: narrow מתאר רוחב, כמו רחוב צר. על בגד שצר עליכם אומרים tight.

options.text: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight around the shoulders.

feedback.en: Clear and specific: what works, what doesn't, and where.
feedback.he: ברור ומדויק: מה מתאים, מה לא, ואיפה.

options.text: Black is good. Navy is not good.

feedback.en: Understandable, but very basic. Say why: 'too tight', 'too long', 'perfect'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל בסיסי מאוד. כדאי להגיד למה: too tight, too long, perfect.

model_replies: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight.
The black one fits really well. The navy's a bit small.

practice.partner: Yeah, that one runs a bit small. Shall I get you the navy in a large?

options.text: No, I don't want. Give me the black.

feedback.en: 'I don't want' needs an object ('I don't want it'), and 'Give me' sounds like an order. Try 'I'll take the black one'.
feedback.he: אחרי I don't want צריך מושא (I don't want it), ו-Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. עדיף I'll take the black one.

options.text: No. Only the black.

feedback.en: Clear, but abrupt. Add 'thanks' and a softer 'That's OK'.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל חד מדי. כדאי להוסיף thanks וגם That's OK כדי לרכך.

options.text: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.

feedback.en: A polite 'no' ('That's OK, thanks') plus a clear decision.
feedback.he: 'לא' מנומס (That's OK, thanks) ואחריו החלטה ברורה.

model_replies: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.
Actually, yes please. Could I try the navy in a large?

roleplay.persona: Priya, a shop assistant in a busy clothes shop in London. Chatty and genuinely helpful, she loves telling customers that something would 'really suit' them.
roleplay.complication: The jacket isn't in stock in the learner's size in the colour they want. Priya can check the stockroom, suggest a similar style or offer to order it in, and she keeps suggesting extra items (a scarf, a matching top) that the learner has to turn down politely.
roleplay.opening_line: Hiya! Are you alright there? Just shout if you need a different size.

culture.en: Shop staff often greet you and offer help. 'I'm just looking, thanks' is a perfectly polite answer, and they'll usually leave you to browse.
culture.he: בחנויות רבות המוכרים יגידו לכם שלום ויציעו עזרה. I'm just looking, thanks היא תשובה מנומסת לגמרי, ובדרך כלל ישאירו אתכם להסתובב בשקט.

culture.en: In the UK, 'Are you alright?' is often just a friendly hello, not a question about your health. 'Yes, thanks' or 'Fine, thanks' is enough.
culture.he: בבריטניה Are you alright? היא הרבה פעמים פשוט ברכה ידידותית, לא שאלה על מצבכם. מספיק לענות Yes, thanks או Fine, thanks.

culture.en: Clothing sizes use different numbers in the UK, the US and Europe, and they vary between brands. Check the label or ask.
culture.he: מידות בגדים מסומנות במספרים שונים בבריטניה, בארה״ב ובאירופה, וגם משתנות בין מותגים. כדאי לבדוק בתווית או לשאול.

variants.note: In the UK, 'pants' means underwear.
'Fitting room' works everywhere.
Where you pay. 'Checkout' works in both.
Spelling only.

scenarios.title_en: Returning an item: refund or store credit?
scenarios.title_he: החזרת מוצר: החזר כספי או זיכוי?

situation.en: Ten days ago you bought a pair of headphones at an electronics store in New York. The left side keeps cutting out. You have the box, but you can't find the paper receipt, only the payment in your banking app. (The store's policy in this scenario is invented for practice.)
situation.he: לפני עשרה ימים קניתם אוזניות בחנות אלקטרוניקה בניו יורק. הצליל באוזנייה השמאלית כל הזמן נקטע. הקופסה אצלכם, אבל את הקבלה המודפסת אתם לא מוצאים, יש רק את התשלום באפליקציה של הבנק. (מדיניות החנות בתרחיש הומצאה לצורך תרגול.)

goal.en: Explain the fault, offer proof of purchase, and politely but firmly push for a refund or a replacement instead of store credit.
goal.he: להסביר מה התקלה, להציג הוכחת קנייה, ולעמוד בנימוס ובתקיפות על החזר כספי או החלפה במקום זיכוי לחנות.

phrases.en: Hi, I'd like to return these, please.
phrases.he: שלום, הייתי רוצה להחזיר את אלה, בבקשה.

phrases.en: They stopped working after about a week.
phrases.he: הן הפסיקו לעבוד אחרי שבוע בערך.

phrases.en: The left side keeps cutting out.
phrases.he: הצליל באוזנייה השמאלית כל הזמן נקטע.
phrases.note: 'Cut out' = suddenly stop working, sometimes coming back on.

phrases.en: I can't find the receipt, but I paid by card. Here's the transaction in my banking app.

situation.en: You're at a crafts market in Mexico City. You love a handwoven blanket, and you'd also like a couple of bracelets as gifts. Nothing has a price tag, and the seller expects some bargaining. (Prices in this scenario are made-up examples.)

goal.en: Ask the price, make a counter-offer and agree on a fair deal for several items, while keeping it friendly.
goal.he: לשאול כמה זה עולה, להציע מחיר נגדי ולהגיע לעסקה הוגנת על כמה פריטים, בלי לאבד את האווירה הנעימה.

model_dialogue.text: Sure, just type your email here. Have a good one!

practice.partner: Hi there. Did you find everything OK?

options.text: Why do you ask me this?

feedback.en: It's just a routine, friendly question, not a real request for information. A suspicious answer sounds strange.
feedback.he: זו שאלת נימוס שגרתית, לא באמת בקשת מידע. תשובה חשדנית נשמעת מוזרה.

options.text: Yes, thanks. Do you have a student discount, by the way?

feedback.en: A quick, friendly answer, then your question. 'By the way' makes it sound relaxed.
feedback.he: תשובה קצרה ונעימה, ואחריה השאלה שלכם. by the way נותן לזה טון רגוע.

options.text: Yes.

feedback.en: Fine, but it can sound cold. 'Yes, thanks' is the usual answer.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל עלול להישמע קר. התשובה הרגילה היא Yes, thanks.

model_replies: Yes, thanks. Do you have a student discount, by the way?
Yes, thank you. Is there a student discount?

practice.partner: We do, ten percent with a student ID. Do you have one with you?

options.text: Yes, I have it. Here is my student identity card.

feedback.en: Correct, but formal. People just say 'student ID' (US) or 'student card' (UK).
feedback.he: נכון, אבל רשמי. אומרים פשוט student ID (ארה״ב) או student card (בריטניה).

options.text: Yes, here you go.

feedback.en: Natural and quick: the cashier can see what you're handing over.
feedback.he: טבעי ומהיר: הקופאי רואה מה אתם מגישים.

options.text: No, but I am student, believe me.

feedback.en: Missing 'a' ('I'm a student'), and asking them to just believe you puts the cashier in an awkward position.
feedback.he: חסר a (I'm a student), ולבקש מהקופאי פשוט להאמין לכם מעמיד אותו במצב לא נעים.

model_replies: Yes, here you go.
Yep, here it is.

practice.partner: Hmm, it says declined. Do you want to try again?

options.text: Your machine is broken.

feedback.en: Blaming their card machine sounds rude, and the problem is often with your bank. Try again or use another card.
feedback.he: להאשים את מכשיר התשלום של החנות נשמע גס, והבעיה היא לעיתים קרובות בבנק שלכם. נסו שוב או השתמשו בכרטיס אחר.

options.text: Yes, again.

feedback.en: Understandable, but abrupt. 'Sure, let me try again' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל חד. Sure, let me try again נשמע נעים יותר.

options.text: That's weird, it worked this morning. Can I insert it instead?

feedback.en: You stay calm, don't blame anyone ('That's weird…') and suggest a solution.
feedback.he: נשארים רגועים, לא מאשימים אף אחד (That's weird...) ומציעים פתרון.

model_replies: That's weird, it worked this morning. Can I insert it instead?
Sure, let me try again.

practice.partner: No, sorry, still declined.

options.text: Sorry about this. I'll pay in cash, then.

feedback.en: A short apology for the delay plus a quick solution. Very natural.
feedback.he: התנצלות קצרה על העיכוב ופתרון מהיר. טבעי מאוד.

options.text: What I do now?

feedback.en: Questions need a helping verb: 'What should I do now?' Better still, suggest another way to pay.
feedback.he: בשאלה צריך פועל עזר: What should I do now? ועוד יותר טוב להציע דרך תשלום אחרת.

options.text: I have cash. I will pay with the cash.

feedback.en: Understandable, but stiff, and 'the cash' sounds odd. 'I'll pay in cash, then' is shorter and more natural.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל נוקשה, ו-the cash נשמע מוזר. I'll pay in cash, then קצר וטבעי יותר.

model_replies: Sorry about this. I'll pay in cash, then.
Sorry! Can I try a different card?

practice.partner: Here's your change. Do you want the receipt in the bag?

options.text: No bag. Email.

feedback.en: Understandable, but too clipped. Make it a request: 'Could you email it to me?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל קטוע מדי. עדיף לנסח כבקשה: Could you email it to me?

options.text: Could you email it to me instead? And no bag, thanks.

feedback.en: Polite request plus a quick 'no bag, thanks'. Exactly how people say it.
feedback.he: בקשה מנומסת ו-no bag, thanks קצר. בדיוק כמו שאומרים את זה.

options.text: I don't need. Give me the check.

feedback.en: 'Check' is the bill at a restaurant (US), not a receipt, and 'I don't need' needs an object: 'I don't need one'.
feedback.he: check זה החשבון במסעדה (בארה״ב), לא קבלה. וגם אחרי I don't need צריך מושא: I don't need one.

model_replies: Could you email it to me instead? And no bag, thanks.
In the bag is fine, thanks.

roleplay.persona: Marcus, a cashier at a busy bookstore in Chicago. Easygoing and patient, he likes chatting about the books people buy, but there's a long line behind the learner.
roleplay.complication: The learner's card is declined twice, and the store's card reader won't accept the learner's second idea, so they need another solution (cash, another card, or putting a book back). The student discount only applies with a valid student ID, and Marcus asks to see it.
roleplay.opening_line: Hi there! Did you find everything OK today?

culture.en: In most US states, the price on the shelf doesn't include sales tax. It's added at the register, so the total is often a little higher than you expect.
culture.he: ברוב מדינות ארה״ב המחיר על המדף לא כולל מס מכירה. המס מתווסף בקופה, ולכן הסכום הסופי לרוב קצת גבוה ממה שציפיתם.

culture.en: If your card is declined abroad, your bank may have blocked the payment as a security check. Check your banking app or call the bank, and carry a backup way to pay.
culture.he: אם הכרטיס נדחה בחו״ל, ייתכן שהבנק חסם את העסקה כבדיקת אבטחה. כדאי לבדוק באפליקציה של הבנק או להתקשר אליו, ותמיד להחזיק אמצעי תשלום נוסף.

culture.en: Cashiers often ask 'Did you find everything OK?' or 'How's your day going?' A short, friendly answer is all they expect.
culture.he: קופאים שואלים הרבה פעמים Did you find everything OK? או How's your day going? מצפים רק לתשובה קצרה ונעימה.

variants.note: 'Checkout' works in both.
Both mean the price is reduced.

scenarios.title_en: Meeting travellers in a hostel

situation.en: You've just arrived at a hostel in Chiang Mai, Thailand. In the common room, a traveller is looking at a map, planning what to do tomorrow. She looks friendly.
situation.he: הגעתם עכשיו להוסטל בצ'יאנג מאי שבתאילנד. בחדר המשותף יושבת מטיילת, מסתכלת על מפה ומתכננת מה לעשות מחר. היא נראית ידידותית.

goal.en: Introduce yourself, talk about your travel plans, and make a plan to do something together tomorrow.
goal.he: להציג את עצמכם, לדבר על תוכניות הטיול שלכם ולקבוע לעשות משהו ביחד מחר.

phrases.en: Hey, mind if I join you?
phrases.note: Very common in hostels. 'Do you mind if I sit here?' is a little more polite. The friendly answer is 'Not at all' or 'Go ahead' (= I don't mind).

phrases.en: Hi, I'm Tal. I just got in today.
phrases.note: 'Get in' = arrive (at a place you're staying).

phrases.en: Where are you from?
How long have you been travelling?
phrases.note: Present perfect continuous: an activity that started in the past and is still going on.

phrases.en: Where are you headed next?
I'm here for about a week, then I'm heading south to the islands.
phrases.he: אני פה בערך שבוע, ואז אני ממשיך/ה דרומה לאיים.

phrases.en: Have you been anywhere good so far?
Any tips for Chiang Mai?
Would you mind if I came along?
phrases.note: 'Come along' = join you. After 'Would you mind if…', use the past simple.

phrases.en: That sounds great, count me in!
What time are you leaving?
Want to swap numbers?
phrases.note: Or: 'Are you on WhatsApp?'

practice.partner: Hi! Are you new? I haven't seen you around.

options.text: Yes. My name is Tal. I am from Israel.

feedback.en: Correct, but it sounds like a textbook. In a hostel, people say 'I'm Tal' and use short forms.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל נשמע כמו ספר לימוד. בהוסטל אומרים I'm Tal ומשתמשים בצורות מקוצרות.

options.text: Yeah, I just got in this afternoon. I'm Tal, from Israel.

feedback.en: Relaxed and friendly: you answer and introduce yourself in one go.
feedback.he: רגוע וידידותי: עונים ומציגים את עצמכם באותה נשימה.

options.text: Yes, I came now.

feedback.en: 'I came now' is a word-for-word translation from Hebrew. Say 'I just got here' or 'I just arrived'.
feedback.he: I came now זה תרגום מילה במילה של 'הגעתי עכשיו'. באנגלית אומרים I just got here או I just arrived.

model_replies: Yeah, I just got in this afternoon. I'm Tal, from Israel.
Yes, I just arrived today. I'm Tal. Nice to meet you!

practice.partner: I'm Lena, from Hamburg. So how long are you in Thailand for?

options.text: I am in Thailand since one week.

feedback.en: This follows Hebrew grammar. English uses the present perfect with 'for': 'I've been in Thailand for a week.'
feedback.he: זה מבנה מהעברית. באנגלית משתמשים ב-present perfect עם for: I've been in Thailand for a week.

options.text: Three weeks.

feedback.en: Correct, but very short. Add a detail and ask her back to keep the conversation going.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל קצר מאוד. כדאי להוסיף פרט ולשאול אותה בחזרה כדי שהשיחה תימשך.

options.text: About three weeks. I'm here for a few days, then I'm heading south. What about you?

feedback.en: A clear plan, natural travel language ('heading south'), and a question back.
feedback.he: תוכנית ברורה, שפת טיולים טבעית (heading south) ושאלה בחזרה.

model_replies: About three weeks. I'm here for a few days, then I'm heading south.
Three weeks in total. I've been here for a week so far. How about you?

practice.partner: I started in Vietnam two months ago. It was amazing.

options.text: Two months, wow! What was your favourite place?

feedback.en: You show interest and ask a follow-up question, which keeps the conversation going.
feedback.he: מראים עניין ושואלים שאלת המשך, וכך השיחה ממשיכה לזרום.

options.text: Nice.

feedback.en: Friendly, but it closes the topic. Add a question like 'What was the best part?'
feedback.he: ידידותי, אבל סוגר את הנושא. כדאי להוסיף שאלה כמו What was the best part?

options.text: I don't like Vietnam.

feedback.en: Negative and a bit rude when she's sharing something she loved. Show interest first.
feedback.he: שלילי וקצת לא נעים כשהיא משתפת במשהו שאהבה. קודם מראים עניין.

model_replies: Two months, wow! What was your favourite place?
That's so cool. What was the best part?

practice.partner: Tomorrow a few of us are doing a cooking class. You should come!

options.text: OK, I will come.

feedback.en: Correct, but flat. Show some enthusiasm: 'I'd love to!' or 'Count me in!'
feedback.he: נכון, אבל יבש. כדאי להראות התלהבות: I'd love to! או Count me in!

options.text: Maybe. How much it costs?

feedback.en: Asking the price is fine, but the question needs 'does': 'How much does it cost?' Show a bit of interest first.
feedback.he: לגיטימי לשאול על המחיר, אבל בשאלה צריך does: How much does it cost? וכדאי קודם להראות קצת עניין.

options.text: Oh, I'd love to! What time does it start?

feedback.en: Warm acceptance plus a practical question.
feedback.he: הסכמה חמה ושאלה מעשית.

model_replies: Oh, I'd love to! What time does it start?
Count me in! How much is it?

practice.partner: They pick us up here at nine. I can ask if there's still space.

options.text: Amazing, thanks! Want to swap numbers so you can let me know?

feedback.en: Natural and practical: you give a reason for asking for her number.
feedback.he: טבעי ומעשי: נותנים סיבה לבקשת המספר.

options.text: OK, bye.

feedback.en: Ends things too suddenly, and you'll have no way to find out if there's space.
feedback.he: מסיים בפתאומיות, ואין לכם דרך לדעת אם נשאר מקום.

options.text: Thank you. Give me your phone number.

feedback.en: Clear, but 'Give me' sounds like an order. Ask: 'Want to swap numbers?' or 'Can I get your number?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. עדיף לשאול: Want to swap numbers? או Can I get your number?

model_replies: Amazing, thanks! Want to swap numbers so you can let me know?
Great, thanks. Are you on WhatsApp?

roleplay.persona: Lena, 24, a traveller from Hamburg on a gap year. Talkative and curious, she's been on the road for two months and loves giving tips.
roleplay.complication: The cooking class turns out to be full. Lena suggests an alternative: an early hike to a waterfall that leaves at 6:30. The learner has to agree on a plan, a time and a meeting place, and swap contacts.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey! Are you new here? I haven't seen you around before.

culture.en: In hostels it's normal to talk to strangers and join their plans. 'Mind if I join you?' is all you need to start.
culture.he: בהוסטלים מקובל לדבר עם זרים ולהצטרף לתוכניות שלהם. Mind if I join you? זה כל מה שצריך כדי להתחיל.

culture.en: Travellers often ask 'Where are you from?', 'How long are you travelling for?' and 'Where are you headed next?' Have a short answer ready, and ask the same question back.
culture.he: מטיילים שואלים הרבה Where are you from?, How long are you travelling for? ו-Where are you headed next? כדאי שתהיה לכם תשובה קצרה מוכנה, ולשאול את אותה שאלה בחזרה.

culture.en: Meeting people on the road is part of the fun, but keep basic safety in mind: meet in public places and tell someone you trust about your plans.
culture.he: היכרויות בדרך הן חלק מהכיף, אבל כדאי לשמור על כללי בטיחות בסיסיים: להיפגש במקומות ציבוריים ולספר למישהו שאתם סומכים עליו על התוכניות שלכם.

variants.note: Spelling only.
Spelling only.
Backpackers on a long trip usually just say 'my trip'.

scenarios.title_en: Small talk at a party

situation.en: You're at a friend's birthday party in London. You only know the host, Sam. A woman is standing near you by the snacks, and you'd like to start a conversation.
situation.he: אתם במסיבת יום הולדת של חבר בלונדון, ומכירים רק את המארח, סאם. לצדכם, ליד שולחן החטיפים, עומדת בחורה, ואתם רוצים לפתוח איתה בשיחה.

goal.en: Start a conversation, keep it going with follow-up questions, and end it politely.
goal.he: לפתוח בשיחה, להמשיך אותה עם שאלות המשך ולסיים אותה בנימוס.

phrases.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Tal.
phrases.he: היי, נראה לי שעוד לא הכרנו. אני טל.

phrases.en: So, how do you know Sam?
phrases.he: אז מאיפה את/ה מכיר/ה את סאם?
phrases.note: The classic opener at a party: everyone there knows the host.

phrases.en: Have you tried these? They're really good.
phrases.he: טעמת את אלה? הם ממש טובים.

phrases.en: Oh really? How did you get into that?
phrases.note: 'Get into' = start doing or liking something.

phrases.en: That sounds amazing. What's it like?
What do you like doing when you're not working?
phrases.he: מה את/ה אוהב/ת לעשות כשאת/ה לא בעבודה?
phrases.note: Friendlier than only asking about someone's job.

phrases.en: Same here!
phrases.note: Shows you have something in common.

phrases.en: No way! I've always wanted to go there.
phrases.he: מה, באמת? תמיד רציתי להגיע לשם.
phrases.note: 'No way!' here shows surprise, not disagreement.

phrases.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
phrases.he: סליחה, לא קלטתי איך קוראים לך.
phrases.note: 'Catch' = hear or understand.

phrases.en: Anyway, I'm going to get a drink. It was really nice talking to you.
phrases.he: טוב, אני הולך/ת להביא משהו לשתות. היה ממש נחמד לדבר איתך.
phrases.note: A natural way to end a conversation at a party.

phrases.en: I'll let you get back to your friends.
phrases.he: לא אעכב אותך, תחזור/י לחברים שלך.
phrases.note: A kind way to end a chat without sounding bored.

phrases.en: Great to meet you. Enjoy the rest of the party!

practice.partner: Oh, hi! I'm Jess. So, how do you know Sam?

feedback.en: Correct, but it gives Jess nothing to continue with. Add a detail or ask her back.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל לא נותן לג'ס במה להמשיך. כדאי להוסיף פרט או לשאול אותה בחזרה.

options.text: Why do you want to know?

feedback.en: Sounds defensive. At a party, this question is just a friendly way to start talking.
feedback.he: נשמע מתגונן. במסיבה זו פשוט דרך ידידותית להתחיל לדבר.

options.text: We're on the same course at uni. What about you?

feedback.en: Answer briefly, then ask the same question back: that's the key to small talk.
feedback.he: עונים בקצרה ושואלים את אותה שאלה בחזרה: זה הסוד של שיחת חולין.

model_replies: We're on the same course at uni. What about you?
We study together. How about you? How do you know him?

practice.partner: Oh, cool! How are you finding London?

options.text: I love it, apart from the weather! How long have you lived here?

feedback.en: A real answer with a light joke, then a question back.
feedback.he: תשובה אמיתית עם קצת הומור, ואחריה שאלה בחזרה.

options.text: I found it on Google Maps.

feedback.en: A misunderstanding: 'How are you finding London?' means 'Do you like it? How is it for you?'
feedback.he: אי-הבנה: How are you finding London? פירושו 'מה דעתך על לונדון?', ולא איך מצאת אותה.

options.text: It is good.

feedback.en: Correct but flat. Add a detail ('apart from the weather', 'the parks are amazing') and a question.
feedback.he: נכון אבל יבש. כדאי להוסיף פרט (apart from the weather או the parks are amazing) ושאלה.

model_replies: I love it, apart from the weather! How long have you lived here?
It's amazing, but really expensive! Are you from London?

practice.partner: I design book covers, mostly. It's fun, but the deadlines are crazy.

options.text: How much money do you make?

feedback.en: Too personal. In most English-speaking cultures, you don't ask about salary when you've just met someone.
feedback.he: אישי מדי. ברוב התרבויות דוברות האנגלית לא שואלים על משכורת מישהו שרק הכרתם.

options.text: Oh wow, that sounds amazing! How did you get into that?

feedback.en: Enthusiasm plus an open question ('How…?') invites a longer answer.
feedback.he: התלהבות ושאלה פתוחה (How...?) מזמינות תשובה ארוכה יותר.

options.text: Do you like your job?

feedback.en: A yes/no question, and she's already told you it's fun. Open questions ('How did you…?', 'What's it like…?') work better.
feedback.he: שאלת כן/לא, והיא כבר אמרה שזה כיף. שאלות פתוחות (How did you...?, What's it like...?) עובדות טוב יותר.

model_replies: Oh wow, that sounds amazing! How did you get into that?
That sounds so interesting. What's the best cover you've done?

practice.partner: I was always drawing as a kid, and it just sort of happened. Do you draw at all?

options.text: No.

feedback.en: Honest, but it stops the conversation. Say what you do instead: 'Not really, I'm more into…'
feedback.he: כנה, אבל עוצר את השיחה. כדאי לספר מה כן: Not really, I'm more into...

options.text: Not really, I'm more into photography. I'd love to see some of your covers, though!

feedback.en: You share something about yourself and show interest in her work.
feedback.he: משתפים משהו על עצמכם ומראים עניין בעבודה שלה.

options.text: No, drawing is for children.

feedback.en: Rude, especially to someone who draws for a living.
feedback.he: גס, במיוחד כלפי מישהי שמתפרנסת מאיור.

model_replies: Not really, I'm more into photography. I'd love to see some of your covers, though!
Not at all, but I love art. Do you have any of your work on your phone?

practice.partner: Anyway, I should go and say hi to Sam's sister. She's just arrived.

options.text: Wait, you didn't tell me how old you are.

feedback.en: Holding someone back with a personal question is awkward. Let her go with a friendly line.
feedback.he: לעכב מישהו עם שאלה אישית זה מביך. עדיף לשחרר אותה במשפט נעים.

options.text: OK. Goodbye, Jess.

feedback.en: Polite, but 'Goodbye' sounds final and formal at a party. 'See you later!' is warmer.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל Goodbye נשמע סופי ורשמי במסיבה. See you later! חם יותר.

options.text: Of course! It was really nice talking to you. See you later!

feedback.en: Warm and natural, and it leaves the door open to talk again.
feedback.he: חם וטבעי, ומשאיר פתח לדבר שוב.

model_replies: Of course! It was really nice talking to you. See you later!
Sure, go ahead! Great to meet you, Jess.

roleplay.persona: Jess, 27, a graphic designer and a colleague of the host. Friendly but a little shy at first; she opens up when people ask real questions about her work and her travels.
roleplay.complication: Jess gives short answers at first, so the learner has to ask open follow-up questions to keep the conversation alive. Later the music gets loud and she mishears something, so the learner has to repeat or rephrase. Finally, the learner should end the chat politely.
roleplay.opening_line: Oh, hi! Are you a friend of Sam's too?

culture.en: Safe small-talk topics: how you know the host, work or studies, travel, food, films and the weather. With someone you've just met, avoid salary, religion and politics.
culture.he: נושאים בטוחים לשיחת חולין: איך מכירים את המארח, עבודה או לימודים, טיולים, אוכל, סרטים ומזג האוויר. עם מישהו שרק הכרתם עדיף להימנע משכר, דת ופוליטיקה.

culture.en: Small talk is like ping-pong: answer, add a detail, then ask something back. One-word answers can seem unfriendly in English.
culture.he: שיחת חולין היא כמו פינג-פונג: עונים, מוסיפים פרט ושואלים משהו בחזרה. באנגלית תשובות של מילה אחת עלולות להיראות לא ידידותיות.

culture.en: At parties, people move on after a few minutes. 'Anyway, it was great talking to you' is a polite way to end a chat; nobody will be offended.
culture.he: במסיבות נהוג לעבור בין אנשים אחרי כמה דקות. Anyway, it was great talking to you היא דרך מנומסת לסיים שיחה, ואף אחד לא ייעלב.

variants.note: Americans often say 'college' even for a university.
'What are you studying?' works everywhere.

scenarios.title_en: Invitations: accepting, declining and rescheduling

situation.en: You're spending a semester in Boston. Your classmate Chris calls to invite you to the movies with some friends on Friday night, but you already have plans that evening.
situation.he: אתם בסמסטר לימודים בבוסטון. חבר לכיתה, כריס, מתקשר להזמין אתכם לסרט עם כמה חברים ביום שישי בערב, אבל באותו ערב כבר יש לכם תוכניות.

goal.en: Decline politely with a reason, suggest another day, agree on the details, and reschedule smoothly if plans change.
goal.he: לסרב בנימוס עם סיבה, להציע יום אחר, לסגור את הפרטים, ולדחות בצורה נעימה אם התוכניות משתנות.

phrases.en: Are you free on Saturday?
Would you like to come to the movies with us?
Do you fancy coming to the cinema with us?
phrases.note: 'Do you fancy…?' is very British.

phrases.en: I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday.
phrases.he: הייתי שמח/ה, אבל ביום שישי אני לא יכול/ה.
phrases.note: 'Make it' = manage to come.

phrases.en: I've already got plans, unfortunately.
How about Saturday instead?
Sounds good! What time works for you?
phrases.he: נשמע טוב! איזו שעה מתאימה לך?

phrases.en: Count me in!
Something's come up. Could we do another day?
phrases.he: צץ לי משהו. אפשר לעשות את זה ביום אחר?
phrases.note: 'Something's come up' = something unexpected has happened. You don't have to explain more.

phrases.en: Can I take a rain check?
phrases.note: = Not this time, but I'd like to another time. Mainly American, but widely understood.

phrases.en: Sorry for the short notice.
Thanks so much for the invite!
phrases.note: 'Invite' as a noun is informal; write 'invitation' in formal messages.

practice.partner: Hey! A few of us are going to the movies on Friday night. Want to come?

options.text: No, I can't. I'm busy.

feedback.en: Honest, but it sounds cold, as if you're not interested. Start with 'I'd love to, but…'
feedback.he: כנה, אבל נשמע קר, כאילו זה לא מעניין אתכם. כדאי להתחיל ב-I'd love to, but...

options.text: Oh, I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday. I've already got plans.

feedback.en: Warm first ('I'd love to'), then a soft no with a short reason. Very natural.
feedback.he: קודם חום (I'd love to), ואחר כך סירוב רך עם סיבה קצרה. טבעי מאוד.

options.text: No, I don't want to go with you.

feedback.en: Very hurtful, even if you're just busy. If you're not interested, use a soft line: 'Thanks, but I'll pass this time.'
feedback.he: פוגע מאוד, גם אם אתם פשוט עסוקים. אם זה לא מעניין אתכם, אפשר לסרב ברכות: Thanks, but I'll pass this time.

model_replies: Oh, I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday. I've already got plans.
Thanks for asking! Friday's tricky for me, though. Could we do another day?

practice.partner: Aw, that's too bad. What about Saturday instead?

options.text: Saturday I can. When it starts?

feedback.en: Word order: 'I can do Saturday', and the question needs 'does': 'When does it start?'
feedback.he: סדר מילים: I can do Saturday, ובשאלה צריך does: When does it start?

options.text: Saturday works! What time were you thinking?

feedback.en: Enthusiastic and moves the plan forward. 'What time were you thinking?' is a soft way to ask.
feedback.he: נלהב ומקדם את התוכנית. What time were you thinking? היא דרך רכה לשאול.

options.text: Yes, Saturday is possible.

feedback.en: Correct, but formal and a bit flat. 'Saturday works!' or 'Saturday's great!' sounds keener.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל רשמי וקצת יבש. Saturday works! או Saturday's great! נשמעים נלהבים יותר.

model_replies: Saturday works! What time were you thinking?
Saturday's great. What time?

practice.partner: Maybe the seven o'clock show, then pizza after?

options.text: Sounds perfect, count me in! Where should we meet?

feedback.en: Clear yes, some enthusiasm, and a practical next step.
feedback.he: 'כן' ברור, קצת התלהבות וצעד מעשי להמשך.

options.text: I will think and I will tell you.

feedback.en: Sounds unsure after you've just said Saturday works, and it's translated word for word from Hebrew. The natural phrase is 'Let me think about it and get back to you', but here it's better to just say yes.
feedback.he: נשמע מהסס אחרי שרק עכשיו אמרתם ששבת מתאימה, וזה תרגום מילולי של 'אחשוב ואגיד לך'. הניסוח הטבעי הוא Let me think about it and get back to you, אבל כאן עדיף פשוט להסכים.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but very minimal for an invitation. Show some enthusiasm.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל מינימלי מדי כתגובה להזמנה. כדאי להראות קצת התלהבות.

model_replies: Sounds perfect, count me in! Where should we meet?
Great, see you there. Should we meet outside?

practice.partner: Hey, are we still on for tonight?

options.text: Oh, I forgot to tell you, I'm not coming.

feedback.en: Cancelling at the last minute with no apology sounds careless. Say sorry and suggest another time.
feedback.he: ביטול ברגע האחרון בלי התנצלות נשמע לא אכפתי. כדאי להתנצל ולהציע מועד אחר.

options.text: I'm so sorry, something's come up and I can't make it tonight. Could we do next weekend instead?

feedback.en: Apologise, give a short reason and suggest a new time right away. It shows you still want to meet.
feedback.he: מתנצלים, נותנים סיבה קצרה ומציעים מיד מועד חדש. זה מראה שאתם עדיין רוצים להיפגש.

options.text: Sorry, I can't come today.

feedback.en: Polite enough, but without a new suggestion it can sound like you don't want to meet. Offer another day.
feedback.he: מנומס מספיק, אבל בלי הצעה חדשה זה עלול להישמע כאילו אתם לא רוצים להיפגש. כדאי להציע יום אחר.

model_replies: I'm so sorry, something's come up and I can't make it tonight. Could we do next weekend instead?
Really sorry, I have to cancel tonight. Can I take a rain check? How about next Saturday?

practice.partner: No worries! Next weekend works for me. I'll let the others know.

options.text: OK, thanks.

feedback.en: Fine, but after cancelling, a bit more warmth helps: 'Thanks for understanding.'
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל אחרי ביטול כדאי קצת יותר חום: Thanks for understanding.

options.text: Maybe. We'll see.

feedback.en: Sounds uncommitted right after you cancelled. Confirm the new plan clearly.
feedback.he: נשמע לא מחויב, ודווקא אחרי שביטלתם. כדאי לאשר את התוכנית החדשה בבירור.

options.text: Thanks for understanding. I'll text you during the week to set a time.

feedback.en: Grateful and committed: you take responsibility for the next step.
feedback.he: מכירים תודה ומראים מחויבות: לוקחים אחריות על הצעד הבא.

model_replies: Thanks for understanding. I'll text you during the week to set a time.
Thanks, Chris. Next weekend it is!

roleplay.persona: Chris, a classmate on the learner's semester in Boston. Easygoing and sociable, always organising group plans, but a bit vague about details.
roleplay.complication: Chris invites the learner for a night they can't make. After they agree on another day, Chris changes the time because of another friend, so the learner has to check whether it works, maybe suggest a different time, and confirm the final plan: day, time and place.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey! What are you up to on Friday night?

culture.en: In English, a direct 'No' to an invitation can sound unfriendly. People soften it ('I'd love to, but…') and suggest another time if they mean it.
culture.he: באנגלית 'לא' ישיר להזמנה עלול להישמע לא ידידותי. נוהגים לרכך (I'd love to, but...) ולהציע מועד אחר אם באמת רוצים.

culture.en: 'What are you up to on Friday?' often comes before an invitation. If you don't know the plan yet, answer 'Nothing much, why?' or 'Why, what's up?'
culture.he: השאלה What are you up to on Friday? באה הרבה פעמים לפני הזמנה. אם עוד לא יודעים מה התוכנית, עונים Nothing much, why? או Why, what's up?

culture.en: If you need to cancel, tell people as early as possible and apologise. Not turning up without a message is considered very rude.
culture.he: אם צריך לבטל, מודיעים כמה שיותר מוקדם ומתנצלים. לא להגיע בלי להודיע נחשב לחוסר נימוס חמור.

variants.us: go to the movies / movie theater
variants.note: 'Movie' is understood everywhere; 'film' is more British.
'Do you want to…?' is used everywhere.

scenarios.title_en: Making friends at a language exchange

situation.en: You're at a language exchange evening in a café in London. People pair up to practise each other's languages. Tonight you're practising with Ben, who is learning Hebrew.
situation.he: אתם בערב חילופי שפות בבית קפה בלונדון. אנשים מתחלקים לזוגות ומתרגלים זה את השפה של זה. הערב אתם מתרגלים עם בן, שלומד עברית.

goal.en: Introduce yourself, ask follow-up questions to get to know Ben, check words you don't understand, and swap contacts so you can meet again.
goal.he: להציג את עצמכם, לשאול שאלות המשך כדי להכיר את בן, לברר מילים שלא הבנתם ולהחליף פרטים כדי להיפגש שוב.

phrases.en: Hi, is this the language exchange?
phrases.he: היי, זה המפגש של חילופי השפות?

phrases.en: How long have you been learning Hebrew?
phrases.he: כמה זמן את/ה כבר לומד/ת עברית?

phrases.en: Why did you decide to learn it?
Your Hebrew is really good!
Sorry, could you say that again?
Could you speak a bit more slowly, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לדבר קצת יותר לאט, בבקשה?

phrases.en: What does 'knackered' mean?
phrases.note: Use this pattern for any new word. ('Knackered' is British slang for 'very tired'.)

phrases.en: How do you say this in English?
phrases.note: Point at something, or say the Hebrew word and ask.

phrases.en: Oh, interesting! What do you like about it?
phrases.he: אה, מעניין! מה את/ה אוהב/ת בזה?

phrases.en: Do you come here every week?
We should practise together again sometime.
phrases.note: UK spelling: 'practise' is the verb, 'practice' the noun. In the US, both are 'practice'.

phrases.en: Are you on Instagram?
phrases.note: Friendlier than 'Give me your Instagram'. Adding a reason ('so we can practise again') keeps it clearly friendly.
